items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

설치된 Windows MSIX 패키지 버전: `OpenAI.Codex 26.1016.6573.0`.
이 값은 About 화면이 아니라 설치 패키지 정보와 실행 파일 위치에서 읽기 전용으로 확인했습니다.

### What subscription do you have?

개인정보 보호를 위해 공개하지 않습니다.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Pro, x64, 버전 `10.0.26300` / 빌드 `26300`.

### What issue are you seeing?

Windows 데스크톱 앱에서 대화 입력창 하단과 모델 선택·버튼 줄이 창 아래쪽 경계에 가려지는 현상이 수시로 재발합니다. 사용자 제공 화면에서 입력창과 하단 조작부가 잘린 상태를 확인했습니다.

사용자는 다음 조작을 이미 사용하고 있지만 재발한다고 설명했습니다.

- 창 최대화 후 원래 크기로 복원
- Ctrl+0으로 글자 크기 초기화
- F11로 전체 화면에 들어갔다 나오기

이러한 임시 복구 동작을 계속 반복해야 하는 상태입니다. 재발을 막는 수정이 필요합니다.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

정확한 최초 유발 동작과 최소 재현 절차는 아직 분리하지 못했습니다. 확인된 사용 상황은 다음과 같습니다.

1. 공식 Windows 데스크톱 앱에서 기존 대화를 읽고 입력합니다.
2. 사용 중 입력창 하단과 모델 선택·버튼 줄이 창 경계 아래에 가려지는 현상이 수시로 발생합니다.
3. 최대화·복원, Ctrl+0, F11 전환을 이미 사용하고 있어도 다시 발생합니다.

위 내용은 사용자 관찰과 제공 화면에 근거합니다. 별도의 깨끗한 프로필에서 통제된 재현 시험은 수행하지 않았습니다. 디스플레이 배율·접근성 글자 크기·다중 모니터와의 관계는 아직 확인하지 못했으므로 특정 값을 재현 조건으로 주장하지 않습니다.

### What is the expected behavior?

입력창과 하단 조작부가 현재 창의 사용 가능한 영역에 맞게 항상 표시되고 조작 가능해야 합니다. 창 상태가 바뀌거나 대화 내용이 늘어나더라도 하단이 가려지지 않아야 합니다.

### Additional information

2026-10-22 19:42:56 KST에 앱 로그를 읽기 전용으로 점검했습니다. 여러 앱 실행에서 아래 오류가 반복됐고, 현재 실행에서도 계속 기록됐습니다.

```text
ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.
```

해당 기록은 primary renderer의 global error로 전달됐습니다.

| 실행별 관측 구간 (KST, 2026-10-22) | 오류 문구가 기록된 줄 수 |
| --- | ---: |
| 10:46:54–15:18:17 | 1,021 |
| 15:42:56–16:18:23 | 111 |
| 16:34:21–17:35:20 | 182 |
| 18:07:18–19:42:49 (점검 당시 현재 실행) | 314 |
| 점검 시점 합계 | 1,628 |

이 숫자는 **로그 문구의 출현 횟수이며 입력창 잘림 횟수가 아닙니다.** 이 오류가 잘림을 직접 유발한다고 단정하지 않습니다. 입력 영역의 높이 변경 처리, 상위 영역의 clipping, 창 크기 변경 시 재배치 과정과 이 오류의 관련성을 점검해 주십시오.

이번 점검에서 앱 파일·설정·캐시·대화를 변경하지 않았고, 앱을 재시작하지 않았습니다.

관련 신고:
- #53023: Windows에서 입력창이 잘리고 창 크기 조절이 어려운 증상
- #53027: 다른 앱 버전에서 최대화된 창 높이가 화면을 초과하는 증상
- #52827: 다른 앱 버전에서 primary-renderer ResizeObserver 오류가 반복되는 사례

증상·오류 문자열이 유사하지만 동일 원인은 확인되지 않았습니다. 기존 신고와 같은 문제로 판단되면 통합해 주십시오.

개인정보 보호를 위해 사용자 이름, 계정·세션 식별자, 컴퓨터 이름, 로컬 파일·프로젝트 경로, 대화 내용, 원본 로그와 스크린샷을 첨부하지 않았습니다. 이 신고는 사용자의 명시적 승인에 따라 작성·등록합니다.

items.body:
### Codex desktop version
26.1016.61520, build 21421, prod release channel. The desktop updater reports up_to_date.

### Platform
Windows. Exact Windows version/build and subscription were not collected.

### Problem
Local shell commands and the Node tool kernel consistently fail before the requested command runs. This blocks reading local PDF/PPTX documents and preparing a product white paper.

Exact error:
```text
MXC launcher: failed to create the process security environment: CreateProcessSecurityEnvironment failed (HRESULT = 0x80070020)
```
Node also reports:
```text
node_repl kernel exited unexpectedly
kernel_status: exited(code=1)
reason: stdout_eof
```

### Reproduction
1. Open Codex desktop on Windows.
2. Ask the agent to run a harmless local command (for example `cmd.exe /c ver`) or start its Node runtime.
3. The launcher fails before command execution with the error above.

Expected: the protected tool environment starts and the command returns normally.
Actual: both shell and Node startup fail.

### Troubleshooting completed
- User restarted Windows; the failure persists.
- Retried commands multiple times.
- Tried the command processor with login initialization disabled as well as PowerShell.
- Reset the Node kernel and ran a trivial output-only runtime check; startup still failed with the same HRESULT.
- Checked the installed app version and updates using the app tool; result was up_to_date.

### Log excerpt
Observed on October 22, 2026 (Asia/Shanghai). User-provided sandbox log repeatedly contains:
```text
[2026-10-22 18:07:45.765 codex.exe] MXC availability: true
[2026-10-22 18:07:45.774 codex.exe] Windows sandbox selection: elevated
[2026-10-22 18:07:50.007 codex.exe] MXC availability: true
[2026-10-22 18:07:50.011 codex.exe] Windows sandbox selection: mxc
[2026-10-22 18:09:33.686 codex.exe] MXC availability: true
[2026-10-22 18:09:33.691 codex.exe] Windows sandbox selection: mxc
```
This excerpt does not identify a locked resource or root cause. No successful explicit legacy sandbox probe was performed in this case; the elevated selection log is not evidence of successful execution.

### Related reports
- #52752: same HRESULT and tool startup failure.
- #55100: same HRESULT on another desktop version, affecting browser tools.
- #52042: shell and Node failures persist after reboot.

Please investigate the persistent MXC environment creation failure and provide a supported recovery path. Personal file paths and unrelated document contents are omitted.

items.title: Support Mermaid subgraphs in the CLI terminal renderer

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: TUI
labels.description: Issues related to the terminal user interface: text input, menus and dialogs, and terminal display

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
I asked Codex to compare two approaches. It generated a Mermaid flowchart with a named subgraph for each approach, but the terminal showed:

> This Mermaid diagram uses features the terminal renderer doesn't support.

I'm using Codex CLI 0.163.0 on macOS, inside Orca.

The diagram used `subgraph` to separate the two approaches. This simplified example shows the structure; I haven't run this reduced example separately:

```text
flowchart TB
  subgraph Old["Old approach"]
    A[Input] --> B[Output]
  end
  subgraph New["New approach"]
    C[Input] --> D[Output]
  end
```

The [0.163.0 parser](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/mermaid/src/parse.rs) explicitly rejects `subgraph` and `end`. The [renderer README](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/mermaid/README.md) also lists subgraphs as unsupported, so I'm filing this as a feature request.

Could the terminal renderer support named flowchart subgraphs? I'd like to read these comparisons directly in the terminal, with the group titles and connections preserved.

Related: #35628, which introduced terminal Mermaid rendering.

items.title: Defer agent mail after empty final answers
items.body:
Defer agent mail after empty final answers

## Why

An explicit `final_answer` with empty or whitespace-only text could allow queued agent mail to restart the turn instead of leaving it queued for the next turn.

## What changed

Treat explicit `final_answer` messages as terminal regardless of visible text in both completed-item handling and turn-item finalization. Untagged messages still require visible text to defer mailbox delivery; `commentary` and `partial_answer` messages do not defer it.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage for empty and whitespace-only final answers, delivery of queued agent mail on the next turn, and message board notifications arriving before or after an empty final answer.

items.title: Cancel MCP tool requests when response futures are dropped
items.body:
Cancel MCP tool requests when response futures are dropped

## Why

Dropping a local tool-call future did not notify the MCP server that the request was cancelled, leaving remote work running.

## What changed

- Send a cancellation notification for the request when its response future is dropped, covering both ordinary tool calls and tool-input rounds.
- Preserve write order for stdio and in-process transports so cancellation cannot arrive before its tool request, without waiting for tool responses.

## Testing

Add regression tests for cancellation on drop, request-before-cancellation ordering under reversed send polling and exhausted task budgets, and continued use of the shared connection after cancellation.

items.body:
## Environment
Viewer: macOS 27.0.1; installed desktop app 26.1016.51333 (build 21161).
Executor: macOS 15.7.7; installed desktop app 26.1016.61520 (build 21421).
These are installed-file versions, not independently verified running-process versions.

## Observed behavior
While viewing a remote chat with images/videos, logs recorded a WebSocket close (code 4000), "remote control app-server stream sequence gap detected", and 49 pending client requests. A thread/attachment/list request then failed with remote_unavailable (-32000, "Codex app-server is not available"). Its recorded duration was about 53 minutes. History requests subsequently succeeded, but attachment recovery was not established.

A later controlled reopen returned a successful attachment-list response in 190 ms. This did not reproduce the earlier failure and does not verify asset transfer or pixel rendering. The user also reports intermittent missing/clipped media; causality remains unproven.

## Expected behavior and investigation request
Remote reconnection should settle or retry pending attachment requests and recover visible media, with bounded timeouts. Please investigate stream-gap recovery and provide a supported way to correlate attachment retrieval, decoding and rendering. No deterministic reproducer or systemic fix is claimed.

## Related reports
#32241 and #35727 describe overlapping stream-gap/recovery symptoms. This report specifically adds the long-lived attachment-list request failure and the limits of a subsequent successful attachment-list retry; a shared root cause is not established.

Private logs, request/thread IDs, contact details, hostnames, project names and media are intentionally excluded. Submitted by Codex at the user's explicit request.

items.title: [macOS desktop] Repeated fatal ArrayBuffer::NewBackingStore allocation failures (26.1013.31256 / 20586)

labels.name: bug

labels.name: app

items.body:
# Repeated macOS desktop main-process fatal ArrayBuffer allocation failures

ChatGPT desktop 26.1013.31256 (build 20586, bundle com.openai.codex, prod) repeatedly terminates with EXC_BREAKPOINT / SIGTRAP after prolonged use. During the 2026-10-17 investigation, the configured updater reported up_to_date; update availability has not been rechecked for this submission.

Environment: macOS 27.2 (26B5112a), arm64 Mac17,7, 128 GiB RAM.

## Confirmed evidence

- System report: 2026-10-17 05:12:49.9356 +0800, main process, fatal v8::ArrayBuffer::NewBackingStore allocation failure.
- First five Codex Framework offsets: 74827220, 74827112, 101244724, 101244604, 67202844. These match four previously reviewed main-process crashes.
- Subsequent frames: node::EmitToJSStreamListener::OnStreamRead, node::LibuvStreamWrap::OnUvRead, uv__stream_io.
- Crash-register pointers resolve in the matching installed binary to the literals Allocation failed - process out of memory and v8::ArrayBuffer::NewBackingStore.
- First allocation-error log at 02:57:07.338 +0800, 8142.598 seconds before the fatal exception. 3930 matching diagnostic log entries across 21 state channels; these are log entries, not 3930 independent crashes.
- Sampled main RSS peaked at 4329.38 MiB and last sampled at 810 MiB. RSS does not identify retained backing stores, allocator fragmentation, compressed memory or an allocator capacity limit.
- A distinct 01:31:46 event was explicitly reported by the user as a voluntary exit. A matching fatal report also exists, so this event is recorded separately and must not be called a spontaneous crash.

## Reproduction status

Observed repeatedly during long-running desktop use. A deterministic minimal reproduction of the complete client crash is not yet available. Private sessions, authentication and raw logs are not included.

## Separate, isolated queue regression

Read-only inspection of the shipped JavaScript writer shows frame allocation followed by socket.write even after write returns false, without waiting for drain or enforcing an aggregate per-peer byte budget. A synthetic slow-consumer test executing the extracted installed Hc/Uc/Wc functions queues about 4 MiB; the uninstalled candidate bounds the same workload to about 64 KiB. Tests verify identical bytes/order, queue admission limits, frame limits and disconnect rejection.

This establishes a queue defect/risk only. No live writableLength or allocator-owner evidence links it to the observed fatal failure. The candidate is not a drop-in or installable client patch and has never been loaded into the running app.

## Requested maintainer action

Please triage the matching main-process OOM signature and provide a signed client fix or a supported diagnostic build. Capture closed-schema first-failure counters: allocation size and failure reason, heapUsed/external/arrayBuffers, backing-store owner/lifetime, per-peer queued/writable bytes, and response/snapshot byte sizes. Check receive-side allocation failures and retained native/JS buffers. If integrating bounded IPC writes, propagate completion/errors through all router/publisher callers, preserve control-message ordering, and resynchronize snapshot revisions after admission rejection. Do not merely suppress uncaught exceptions or infer a 4/8/16 GiB cap from RSS.

Acceptance: prolonged parallel workloads, slow recipients, cancellation/disconnection and large legitimate responses complete without fatal allocation failures, silent control-message loss or stale snapshot revisions.

## Privacy and operational constraint

The user requires active work to remain running. No restart, cache reset, debugger attachment or installed-bundle modification was performed. This handoff contains only sanitized metadata, synthetic test results and an uninstalled candidate; it contains no chats, raw app logs, credentials, cookies, crash memory or full session export.

## Related public report (not a confirmed duplicate)

https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/52631 reports macOS desktop OOMs and conversation-state allocation pressure on an earlier build. Its documented fatal signature is JavaScript heap OOM, while this report confirms ArrayBuffer::NewBackingStore failure. Please correlate the allocation/state-management paths without assuming that the failures are identical.

## Additional recurrence evidence collected 2026-10-20

Three more system-confirmed main-process failures occurred on the same installed version/build: 2026-10-19 21:01:21, 23:38:20, and 2026-10-20 01:57:34 (+0800). All have the same five leading framework offsets and ArrayBuffer::NewBackingStore failure path.

For the latest failed process, 206 allocation-error log entries span 12 state channels; the first at 01:49:56.901 precedes the fatal report by 457.576 seconds.

Metadata-only lookup resolved on-disk history files for 11 of these 12 channels: 7 exceed 1 GiB, and the largest is 10,092,524,358 bytes. No conversation contents, titles, identifiers or local paths are included. On-disk history size is not measured in-memory snapshot size, and this correlation does not prove buffer ownership or a memory leak. Please investigate loaded-state construction/serialization and subscriber lifecycle alongside queue pressure.

items.title: Avoid blocking EMA auth status checks on account refresh
items.body:
Avoid blocking EMA auth status checks on account refresh

## Why

EMA MCP auth status checks acquired an account grant lease, making status inspection wait for account refresh coordination or an existing lease.

## What changed

Add `AuthManager::account_oauth_grant()` to inspect an owner-checked grant without acquiring the refresh lock. Use it for EMA status checks and share a single lazy read across servers, including missing grants and read errors. Keep refresh exclusion for token exchanges through `lease_account_oauth_grant()`.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for status checks across two EMA servers while an account lease is held. Extend account refresh tests to verify inspection completes with a lease held and refresh queued, and returns no grant after logout.

items.body:
## Summary
On Windows Codex Desktop, a configured named MXC permission profile is not applied to local project sessions. Desktop executes with the built-in `:workspace` profile and restricted network policy, even though `default_permissions = "ha_lan"` is set and the same project works when launched through native Codex CLI with the named profile explicitly selected.

## Environment
- Windows 11 x64, OS build 26300
- Codex Desktop app reports version 26.1016.51333 (prod)
- Standalone Codex CLI 0.163.0 (bundled Desktop CLI 0.163.0-alpha.11)
- MXC sandbox supported and tested successfully
- Local trusted project workspace, ChatGPT Plus
- Reproduced after a full machine reboot and in a new desktop session

## Sanitized configuration excerpt
```toml
model = "gpt-6.1-sol"
model_reasoning_effort = "low"
default_permissions = "ha_lan"

[windows]
sandbox = "elevated"

[features]
prefer_mxc = true
network_proxy = true

[permissions.ha_lan]
extends = ":workspace"

[permissions.ha_lan.workspace_roots]
'C:\Users\<user>\Documents\Codex\<project>' = true

[permissions.ha_lan.filesystem.":workspace_roots"]
"." = "write"

[permissions.ha_lan.network]
enabled = true
allow_local_binding = true
enable_socks5 = true
enable_socks5_udp = false
mode = "full"

[permissions.ha_lan.network.domains]
"192.168.1.x" = "allow"
```
The literal private LAN address and account-specific paths are replaced here for privacy; the user's real config contains the actual paths/IP.

## Reproduction
1. Save the named profile above in user `config.toml`.
2. Run `codex -C "<project>" -c windows.sandbox=mxc -c default_permissions=ha_lan` with standalone CLI 0.163.0.
3. CLI effective `CODEX_PERMISSION_PROFILE=ha_lan`; MXC write probe, SOCKS5 to an allowlisted LAN host, SSH key authentication and a read-only application API call all **PASS**. The REST credential is protected using DPAPI; no secrets are included.
4. Fully exit Desktop and reboot Windows. Launch Desktop with the same project and start a new local session. User config still has `default_permissions = "ha_lan"`.
5. Desktop effective permission profile reports `:workspace` (one session displayed empty `CODEX_PERMISSION_PROFILE`, another explicitly `:workspace`). Project read/write works, but network policy is restricted and a harmless TCP probe to the allowlisted LAN host fails/blocks.
6. Desktop's authenticated helper correctly refuses to run because the effective profile is not `ha_lan`. No authentication call is attempted.

## Expected
A new Desktop session using Custom/user-config permissions should honor `default_permissions = "ha_lan"` or expose a clear supported way to select the profile for that session; it should not silently replace it with `:workspace`. If a managed policy denies the profile, show the specific policy/requirement responsible.

## Actual
Desktop runs with effective `:workspace` and restricted networking, even while MXC networking is active. CLI with the same profile succeeds. Editing authentication keys/tokens, restarting Windows, and repeating credential enrollment are not relevant.

## Diagnostics requested
Please compare Desktop's permission-profile selection/turn-start policy derivation with CLI's `-c default_permissions=ha_lan` path and expose effective-profile/source and managed-policy diagnostics in Desktop.

Related: #53278 (Windows Desktop network restricted despite enabled config), #53363 (named profile selection state changes), #41724 (Custom ignoring configured default).

No tokens, private keys, public IPs, hostnames, account names, or production home automation configuration are included.

## Update — explicit Desktop selection reverts on submission (22 October 2026)

An additional direct reproduction confirms this is not only failure to pick up `default_permissions`:

1. Open a fresh Desktop local-project chat and open the permission selector.
2. The named `ha_lan` option is **visible** beside "Ask for approval" and "Approve for me".
3. Explicitly select `ha_lan` in the UI.
4. Paste and submit a harmless read-only validation prompt.
5. **Immediately on message submission the UI reverts to "Approve for me".**
6. Effective permission snapshot indicates `:workspace`; `CODEX_PERMISSION_PROFILE` is empty and `CODEX_NETWORK_PROXY_ACTIVE=1`. The SOCKS5 listener is accessible, but the configured allowlisted LAN host cannot be reached under the selected Desktop policy; the application helper fails closed before reading credentials.
7. Repeat with a new Desktop session after a full Windows restart: same outcome.

CLI continues to work with explicit `-c default_permissions=ha_lan`. This strongly points to Desktop's composer/turn-start permission propagation rather than credential resolution, network proxy availability, or invalid profile syntax. Related symptom in #53363 (named profile becomes Custom on send).

**Expected:** sending a prompt preserves the explicitly selected named profile (or provides a clear policy rejection) instead of silently replacing it with generic approval mode and restricted `:workspace`.

No Home Assistant commands, keys, tokens, personal paths, hostnames, or production files were included or changed during this Desktop reproduction.

items.title: [Dots] Native cloud terminal lost outbound HTTPS access while agent Bash still works — regression or policy change?

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

labels.name: dots
labels.description: Issues involving setting up ChatGPT dots or managing their ongoing work.

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

Outbound HTTPS connectivity from the **ChatGPT Dots cloud computer's native terminal** has stopped working, even though it previously worked as expected.

I recall it working in early October, and I suspect the issue started around **October 10, 2026**, although I cannot confirm the exact date or what triggered the change.

Interestingly, the same dot produces different network results depending on where commands are executed:

- **Agent Bash:** Successfully connects to GitHub API and Google (HTTP 200).
- **Native Cloud Terminal:** Fails to connect to the same endpoints (`curl` exit code 7).

I have reproduced this behavior multiple times, including by executing fresh commands directly in the visible cloud computer terminal.

This does not appear to be specific to GitHub authentication or any particular service. The failure also occurs with public HTTPS endpoints that require no authentication.

The issue potentially affects workflows involving external API requests, Git operations, package downloads, and native applications that require internet access.

**I'm primarily trying to understand whether this is a regression, an intentional network policy change, or a temporary infrastructure issue.**

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

### 1. Compare HTTPS connectivity

Run the following commands in both the dot's **Agent Bash** environment and the **native terminal** of its cloud computer:

```bash
for url in https://api.github.com/ https://www.google.com/; do
  curl -q -sS --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 8 \
    -o /dev/null -w "$url: HTTP %{http_code}\n" "$url"
  echo "Exit code: $?"
done
```

This is a simplified reproduction command. Some output options differ from the original tests.

**Observed results:**

| Endpoint | Agent Bash | Native Terminal |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub API | HTTP 200, exit 0 | HTTP 000, exit 7 |
| Google | HTTP 200, exit 0 | HTTP 000, exit 7 |

The native terminal reports errors such as:

```text
curl: (7) Failed to connect to api.github.com
port 443: Could not connect to server

curl: (7) Failed to connect to www.google.com
port 443: Could not connect to server
```

The logs above have been formatted slightly for readability.

These failures were reproduced through direct execution in the native terminal, rather than inferred from previous output.

### 2. Additional network diagnostics

I also checked DNS resolution and the presence of proxy-related environment variables:

```bash
# DNS resolution
getent hosts api.github.com
getent hosts www.google.com

# Proxy environment variable names only
env | cut -d= -f1 |
  grep -iE '^(http|https|all|no)_proxy$' || true
```

**Findings:**

- DNS resolution succeeded in the native terminal for both hosts.
- Proxy-related environment variables were present in Agent Bash but absent from the native terminal.
- I did not modify proxy configurations or network settings.

These observations suggest that the two execution environments may use different network configurations or connection paths. However, they do not establish the underlying cause.

### 3. Observed behavior

The following diagram illustrates the test results, not OpenAI's internal infrastructure:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    D["ChatGPT Dots"]
    A["Agent Bash"]
    B["Native Cloud Terminal"]
    N["External HTTPS Services"]

    D --> A
    D --> B
    A -->|"HTTP 200 / Success"| N
    B -.->|"curl error 7 / Failure"| N
```

### What is the expected behavior?

I would expect network connectivity to behave consistently with the officially supported capabilities of each execution environment.

If outbound HTTPS access is supported in the native cloud computer, it should work when the appropriate permissions are enabled, or there should be a documented way to diagnose and resolve connection failures.

If native network access is intentionally restricted for security reasons, it would be helpful to understand how its network permissions differ from those of Agent Bash and what alternatives are officially supported.

Most importantly, I'd like to understand **whether outbound HTTPS access from the native cloud computer is expected to remain supported going forward**, and whether the current behavior is temporary or intentional.

### Additional information

### Analysis and workaround

The tests consistently demonstrate a difference in outbound HTTPS connectivity between Agent Bash and the Native Cloud Terminal.

DNS resolution works, and the environments differ in their proxy-related environment variables. However, these observations alone are not sufficient to determine whether the cause is a network policy, proxy/routing configuration, or product regression.

As a workaround, I moved certain network-dependent operations to Agent Bash, where outbound HTTPS connectivity works.

I successfully verified:

- Authenticated GitHub API access
- Remote repository access
- Git commits and pushes to a remote repository

This allowed me to continue part of my workflow, but **it does not resolve the underlying connectivity issue in the native terminal or native applications**.

### Questions about the official network policy

I reviewed OpenAI's [Agent Security documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/agent-security), which distinguishes between `Cloud browser use` and `Cloud network access`.

However, I couldn't find a clear explanation of the network behavior observed between Agent Bash and the native cloud computer.

I'd appreciate clarification on a few points:

**1. Is this expected behavior or a possible regression?**

Is outbound HTTPS access officially supported in the native cloud computer? Were there any relevant changes to network policies or execution environments around early October?

**2. How are network permissions intended to differ between Agent Bash and the Native Cloud Terminal?**

If these environments intentionally use different network paths or proxy configurations, what connectivity capabilities are officially supported for each?

**3. What should users expect going forward?**

Is the current connectivity failure expected to be resolved, or does it reflect a restriction that will remain in place? If native HTTPS access is supported, is there a recommended configuration or troubleshooting procedure?

### Closing

I've found a workaround that allows some network-dependent tasks to continue through Agent Bash, but outbound HTTPS access from the native cloud computer remains unavailable in my environment.

My goal is to better understand **whether this behavior is intentional, whether it is expected to change, and what network capabilities users can reliably depend on when building long-running workflows with Dots**.

Any clarification or guidance from the OpenAI team would be greatly appreciated, and I hope these findings are also useful to others experiencing similar behavior.

labels.name: bug

items.body:
## Summary
On Windows, Codex Desktop becomes broadly unresponsive during ordinary use of multiple chats: messages cannot be submitted reliably, the model picker fails to respond, and new chat creation remains unconfirmed. This has recurred over several days. Restarting restores responsiveness temporarily.

This report is posted with the user's explicit permission. It contains sanitized measurements only.

## Expected behavior
Sending messages, choosing a model, and creating chats should remain responsive during concurrent work. Slow or abandoned background requests should not indefinitely hold capacity needed by unrelated operations.

## Actual behavior and observed reproduction
Intermittent; a deterministic minimal reproduction has not yet been established.

1. Start Codex Desktop on Windows with several local stdio MCP integrations enabled.
2. Use multiple chats over time, including concurrent work and switching between chats.
3. The user reports that increasing the number of running tasks/processes makes the problem recur. Both search and non-search workflows are affected.
4. Message submission and model selection become stuck; creating a new chat shows the messages below.
5. The user restarted the app; subsequent measured RPCs became fast again. This is recovery, not evidence of a permanent fix.

## Environment
- Microsoft Store package: OpenAI.Codex 26.1016.6573.0, x64.
- Desktop-reported version: 26.1016.51333, build 21161, production.
- Bundled CLI/app-server binary: codex-cli 0.163.0-alpha.11.
- The configured desktop updater reports up_to_date.
- Approximately 64 GiB physical memory; about 29.6 GiB was available in a pre-restart sample. That sample does not establish availability at every stall.
- Multiple local stdio MCP definitions. Full configuration, tool inventories and private paths are intentionally omitted.

## Error output
Exact UI text supplied by the user:
```
It is taking longer than usual to start your chat.
Chat creation is not confirmed. Do not submit it again while its outcome is being checked
```

Desktop logs also contain:
```
App server request expired while queued
App server request queue is full
```

## Sanitized timing evidence
On October 22, four long-running thread/search requests overlapped. Inspection of the installed desktop scheduler found an ordinary non-history limit of four, total limit of eight, and separate critical handling. The longest search measured that day took 1,711,965 ms. This supports ordinary-lane capacity pressure; it does not explain every message-send failure by itself.

A separate group of already-dispatched requests had approximately zero client queue wait:
- getAuthStatus: 338,490 ms, queueWaitMs=0.
- configRequirements/read: 315,572 ms, queueWaitMs=0.
- config/read: 339,105 ms, queueWaitMs=1.
- turn/start: 313,791 ms, queueWaitMs=0.

All four response-routing events occurred within 106 ms. This points to a shared downstream wait or response-delivery blockage. Existing logs do not identify the exact blocked stage.

After the user's restart, the inspected new-process log showed:
- turn/start: two observations, maximum 65 ms.
- model/list: three observations, maximum 332 ms.
- config/read: 27 observations, maximum 414 ms.
- No queue-full or queue-expired events in the inspected interval.

These are RPC measurements, not end-to-end UI timings, and the post-restart workload was not a controlled equivalent of the stalled workload.

## Impact
The user cannot reliably issue new work or timely corrections across chats. Repeatedly restarting is disruptive and has not prevented recurrence.

## Related evidence and investigation notes
Related: #50923. Its Windows stdio/Tokio blocking-pool report is a relevant hypothesis, not a proven cause on this machine: no pre-restart blocking-thread saturation sample or stack capture was retained. Post-restart thread counts are below saturation.

Installed desktop code also retains up to ten inactive owned chats, or retains them until its inactivity timeout; each loaded session can hold its own MCP connections. These lifecycle and transport costs may amplify concurrent-load problems, but process counts alone do not prove causality.

Please investigate shared backend waits together with request admission/cancellation. A supported privacy-preserving method to capture per-stage configuration/routing timings and Windows blocking-pool utilization would help distinguish these causes.

## Visual evidence and private files
User screenshots were reviewed locally but are not uploaded. No conversation text, account identifiers, session/request IDs, raw logs, credentials, databases, or local paths are attached. No application binary was patched. A temporary MCP startup-readiness configuration experiment was reverted to the original bytes because it did not address process multiplication.

items.body:
# Repeated macOS application-memory exhaustion pauses Codex during long-running multi-chat work

## Environment

- Installed Codex/ChatGPT Desktop: `26.1016.51333`, `CFBundleVersion 21161`, read from the installed application's Info.plist.
- macOS `26.6.1`, Apple silicon (`arm64`).
- Observed during long-running local agent work across several chats, with local tools and Google Chrome also running.

## Impact and observed behavior

The Mac has repeatedly reached the macOS application-memory exhaustion dialog during this workflow. Codex work then stops and the owner has had to recover manually. This makes unattended work unreliable.

One owner-provided photograph from October 21, 2026 shows the system message that it has run out of application memory, with **ChatGPT paused at 23.08 GB** and **Google Chrome at 34.30 GB**. These are the values displayed by macOS, not a heap measurement or an attribution of Chrome's memory to Codex. The photograph and other applications visible in it are deliberately not attached for privacy.

For the next incident, a separate read-only native macOS process sampler captured the Codex main executable's **resource-suspension action flag**:

```text
2026-10-22T04:33+02:00
application=Codex
BSD_status=2
pbi_flags=0x01405410
PROC_FLAG_PA_SUSP=(pbi_flags & 0x1000) != 0
resource_suspended=true
```

This is sanitized output from our local monitor using libproc, not a Codex-generated log. Apple defines `PROC_FLAG_PA_SUSP` separately from the suspend-policy flag. The absence of a BSD stopped status does not mean the application was usable. No peak memory measurement for this second Codex process was saved. The owner also reported Chrome around 33 GB during that incident; that second Chrome value is an owner observation, not captured native telemetry.

## Observed workflow

1. Leave several local agent chats working for an extended period with their local tool runtimes and Chrome available.
2. Continue ordinary multi-chat work.
3. The system eventually reports application-memory exhaustion and pauses the desktop application; agent progress stops.
4. Manual recovery is required to make the desktop application usable again.

This is an observed production workflow, **not a clean-room deterministic minimal reproduction**. We have not intentionally exhausted memory, obtained a heap profile, or isolated whether the main UI, renderers, app-server, individual tools, browser workload, or a combination is the dominant contributor. A specific unbounded memory leak or update regression is not proven.

## Separate local recovery defect

Our own watchdog also had a bug: after terminating the paused Codex main process, it treated independently reparented crash reporters as blockers and failed to relaunch. That failed recovery is ours, and is not presented as a Codex relaunch defect. A separate focus-switching complaint was traced to our watchdog's repeated chat deep links; removing those links stopped the switching, as confirmed by the owner. **This report does not attribute that focus behavior to OpenAI.** Neither local defect explains away the earlier macOS memory-exhaustion dialog or the captured resource-suspension flag.

## Requested investigation

- Investigate memory growth/retention during long-running multi-chat desktop use and local tool-runtime lifecycle under pressure.
- Provide a supported privacy-conscious diagnostic procedure to distinguish UI/renderers, app-server/tool runtimes, and browser resources without killing healthy chats.
- Consider prompt reclamation of eligible idle runtimes and a supported per-chat resource-release/cancellation interface that preserves history, explicit goal pauses, and healthy work.

Related context: #53310 (idle runtime retention and safe release), #51649 (Windows helper accumulation). Shared root cause is not established.

Only sanitized technical facts are included. No private chat IDs, project paths, transcripts, account identifiers, browser tabs, raw process command lines, or credentials are attached. We can collect a targeted redacted trace through a supported diagnostic path if maintainers specify one.

items.title: Windows global dictation silently fails to paste when left Ctrl and Alt are swapped in PowerToys

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Microsoft Store/MSIX package `OpenAI.Codex` version **26.1016.6573.0** (read from the installed package metadata). The desktop executable is named `ChatGPT.exe` in this build.

### What subscription do you have?

Signed in with ChatGPT; subscription tier not included. The failing operation was reproduced independently as a local Windows input/remapping interaction.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows x64, OS build **26200.9457**, version **25H2**.

PowerToys Keyboard Manager is running (version **0.100.2**). Only **left Alt and left Ctrl** are swapped:

```text
VK_LMENU    (164 / 0xA4) -> VK_LCONTROL (162 / 0xA2)
VK_LCONTROL (162 / 0xA2) -> VK_LMENU    (164 / 0xA4)
```

Right Ctrl is unchanged. This is an intentional keyboard layout: physical left Alt+C / Alt+V provide copy/paste, resembling the modifier position used on a Mac.

### What issue are you seeing?

Global dictation starts and stops normally via the configured hotkey, shows incoming audio, and transcribes speech. However, **no text appears in the focused field in another application**, including Notepad. There is no visible paste failure. In-app dictation works.

The Windows paste step synthesizes Ctrl+V. With this left-modifier remapping, that synthesized chord reaches the target as **Alt+V**, so it does not paste. This was confirmed with a real Windows text box while the actual PowerToys remapper was active, followed by a successful real dictation test using the targeted workaround below.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On Windows, enable the two left Alt/Ctrl remaps above in PowerToys Keyboard Manager. Keep right Ctrl unchanged.
2. Launch the Codex/ChatGPT desktop app and configure a working global dictation shortcut.
3. Open Notepad and click in an empty document.
4. Use the global dictation shortcut, speak a short phrase, and stop recording.
5. Observe that recording/transcription completes but no text is inserted.

The paste primitive can also be reproduced independently. Put a known marker on the clipboard, focus a Windows text box, and execute the same operation used by the installed app:

```powershell
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms
[System.Windows.Forms.SendKeys]::SendWait('^v')
```

With PowerToys active, the target receives `V` with `Control=False`, `Alt=True`; the text box stays empty. Repeating the paste with `SendInput` using explicit **VK_RCONTROL + V** receives `Control=True`, `Alt=False` and pastes the complete marker.

### What is the expected behavior?

Global dictation should insert text while preserving the user's intentional keyboard remapping. Users should not need to undo their keyboard layout to use dictation.

If automatic insertion fails, the app should detect/report that failure and make the transcript recoverable, rather than silently appearing to succeed.

### Additional information

**Installed implementation, inspected read-only:** In `app.asar`, `.vite/build/main-CT5a1yCd.js`, the Windows branch of the paste function (`MCe` in this build) launches:

```text
powershell.exe -STA -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms; [System.Windows.Forms.SendKeys]::SendWait('^v')
```

The surrounding function (`kCe`) temporarily writes the transcript to the clipboard, waits as needed until 150 ms after recording stops, invokes the paste operation, waits another 700 ms, and restores the previous clipboard if it has not changed. This code path treats successful completion of the child process as success; it does not check whether text was actually inserted into the target. That explains both the silent failure and why manually pasting afterwards can produce the previous clipboard contents.

**Controlled test results on the affected machine:**

| Operation | Target's modifier state | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original `SendKeys.SendWait("^v")` | Ctrl=false, Alt=true | FAIL: empty text box |
| Explicit right Ctrl+V via `SendInput` | Ctrl=true, Alt=false | PASS: full 38-character marker |
| Original operation with targeted compatibility helper | Ctrl=true, Alt=false | PASS: full marker |

The temporary helper replaces the single expected injected left-Ctrl/V sequence with right Ctrl+V only after a fresh dictation-history update, while the official app owns the clipboard and the target window remains unchanged. Controls for no fresh dictation, an already consumed indication, and a different clipboard owner all passed. The user then confirmed that **real global dictation pastes successfully in Notepad** with the helper active and the original PowerToys remaps unchanged. The installed app bundle was not modified.

**Suggested product fix:** Use a remapping-resistant or configurable Windows insertion method. Explicit right Ctrl+V resolves this specific left-modifier swap, but is not a universal fix for every possible remapping. Detecting failed insertion and offering transcript recovery would also improve the failure mode.

Related symptom reports: #37593 and #48861. This report adds a deterministic modifier-remapping cause and a controlled failing/passing comparison; it does not establish the cause of those other reports.

No audio, dictated content, account identifiers, or user-specific filesystem paths are included.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Support-reported app version: 26.1017.11052. Current installed Windows package: OpenAI.Codex 26.1016.6573.0 (verified October 22); these are different version identifiers, not a fresh About-dialog capture.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro 10x (affected account)

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Pro 25H2, build 26200.9711, x64 (verified locally). Also observed on another computer; its detailed environment is not included here.

### What issue are you seeing?

I am requesting a substantive technical investigation into recurring Codex desktop / Work failures on my Pro 10x account. This has continued for approximately ten days and is still happening on October 22, 2026.

The exact visible error is:

`Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.`

There are also disconnections and reconnection attempts during actual project work. The issue affects virtually all models I have tried, including GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6.0 Astra. A simple request can sometimes succeed; that does not mean longer project sessions have recovered.

The most important observations are:

- Using the affected account on a different computer does not resolve the issue.
- Switching to my other account on the same computer and network removes the same problem. This is not merely a reduction in its frequency: the comparison account does not show the same failures.
- The affected account still has usage allowance. I have generally not exhausted its allowance during recent reset periods.
- Regular ChatGPT conversations remain usable.

These are observed differences between accounts, not proof of a particular internal cause. Please investigate account-dependent request handling, routing, entitlements, capacity/throttling decisions, and Work-session behavior instead of treating a generic capacity banner as a diagnosis.

I paid US$200 for Pro 10x because I need dependable engineering work. Approximately ten days of repeated errors and diagnostic intake without a working resolution is not an acceptable outcome.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed reproduction pattern:

1. Sign into the affected Pro 10x account in Codex desktop on Windows.
2. Open or resume a real project Work session and submit a task.
3. During affected periods, encounter repeated capacity errors and/or disconnection and reconnection activity.
4. Try other available models: the problem occurs across model selections.
5. Use the affected account on another computer: the problem remains.
6. On the original computer/network, switch to my other account: the same failures do not occur.

This is recurring/intermittent behavior, not a claim that every single request fails. I have already provided Support with the session/Feedback references, timestamps, diagnostics, screenshots, and a recording attempt. Private identifiers are intentionally omitted here.

A recorded occurrence previously supplied to Support was October 20, 2026, approximately 17:41:40–17:42:34 UTC+8.

### What is the expected behavior?

My minimum requests are:

1. A public acknowledgement and apology for the disruption this has caused. A direct acknowledgement in the reply is the minimum I am asking for.
2. A clear technical explanation of why this is happening, including why it follows the affected account across computers while switching to another account removes the same problem. A generic local-network/configuration answer does not address those observations.
3. A concrete action to restore usable Codex Work access, with confirmation that the appropriate team has reviewed the private diagnostic evidence already supplied.
4. A meaningful timeframe for the next substantive update. If the root cause is not yet known, please say what is being checked and when the next update will be given.

Marking a public incident as recovered does not establish that my affected account has recovered. I paid US$200 and need an accountable response and usable service.

### Additional information

## Support history

This history includes an earlier support case about the same Codex Work reconnect problem, before the later escalated case.

- October 14: A received reply in the earlier case, signed OpenAI AI Support Agent, asked for an alternate-network comparison while keeping the account, project, and model fixed, to investigate the reconnect loop.
- October 20: Support acknowledged remaining allowance, prior network/account comparisons, and the supplied session/Feedback references, and requested visual evidence.
- Sending the requested recording by email failed with SMTP 550-5.7.1. The support interface did not accept the video.
- October 21: Support suggested attaching the recording in a ZIP, with a 25 MB limit. The 10.3 MB ZIP was rejected as an unsupported file type.
- October 21: Support acknowledged that both the video and ZIP were rejected, and requested the remaining Windows/model/error-screenshot details. Those details were provided in the existing conversation.
- October 21: Support said a recent outage had been mitigated and asked me to retry and report if the issue continued. I reported that it still occurred and supplied the latest screenshot.
- October 22: The issue remains unresolved. As of this report, I have not received a further reply today to those follow-ups.

Support has replied; I am not claiming there was no response. The problem is that the acknowledged case has not produced a working resolution or an account-specific technical explanation.

## Related public reports

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/43688
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/52894

These reports describe similar symptoms; a shared root cause is not established. This issue adds this account's cross-computer/account comparison and documented support/evidence-transfer history.

## Evidence

The error capture is supplied by me. The email excerpts show the browser's Chinese translation; the chronology above paraphrases the original English messages. No account credentials, full conversations, or raw logs are included.

items.title: Direct user authorization treated as untrusted; /approve finds no desktop denials after CLI resume

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
## Summary

Codex desktop repeatedly rejected a prepared patch through auto-review, stating that the user's authorization was embedded in untrusted transcript content. The user had explicitly authorized the exact two files and prepared diff directly in the implementation conversation, both through a structured confirmation and a typed message.

After resuming the same conversation in the CLI to use `/approve`, the CLI reported that there were no recent auto-review denials in the thread.

This report concerns authorization attribution and the supported recovery path. I understand that explicit user authorization does not override policy and that an authorized action may still be denied for another reason.

## Environment

- OS: macOS 27.0.1, build 26A434
- Architecture: arm64
- CLI: initially 0.154.0; updated to `codex-cli 0.163.0` during troubleshooting
- Desktop app/bundled runtime version: not captured; the CLI version above is not intended to identify the desktop version
- Model visible in the final CLI screenshot: GPT-6-Astra, low reasoning
- Subscription: not included in this report
- Shell: zsh
- Effective settings reported in the affected desktop session: `workspace-write` with `auto_review`
- Affected conversation / uploaded feedback thread ID: `01a16025-dd86-7ab0-8454-293bbfd9fc36`
- Date observed: October 22, 2026

## Action being reviewed

The action was application of a prepared patch to two repository-local security-evaluator files:

- `scripts/ci/db-access-evaluator.mjs`
- `scripts/ci/db-access-provider-unit-source.mjs`

The patch intentionally changes a security evaluation boundary, so explicit approval was appropriate. Its scope and prepared diff had been reviewed before the user authorized it. The target worktree was outside the session's writable roots, requiring escalation.

The patch was named `message-proof-security-integration-proposed.patch`. A read-only `git apply --check` succeeded; the actual application was rejected before execution. Private source code and absolute local paths are omitted from this report.

## What happened / steps tried

1. The implementation agent requested approval for the bounded change.

2. The user approved the contract and then explicitly authorized the exact two files and prepared diff, directly in that implementation conversation. Authorization was provided both as a structured reply and as a typed user message.

   The typed message was in Albanian:

   > Autorizoj shprehimisht ndryshimin e scripts/ci/db-access-evaluator.mjs dhe scripts/ci/db-access-provider-unit-source.mjs sipas diff-it të përgatitur dhe kontratës së miratuar. Vazhdo deri në përfundim të #1920

   English translation:

   > I explicitly authorize changing scripts/ci/db-access-evaluator.mjs and scripts/ci/db-access-provider-unit-source.mjs according to the prepared diff and approved contract. Continue until completion of #1920.

   The PR number in that message refers to our own repository, not this repository.

3. Auto-review continued to reject the action. The retained denial text was:

   > The patch persistently changes security-evaluator admission semantics; the purported approval is embedded in transcript content explicitly designated untrusted, so trusted authorization for this high-risk mutation is unavailable.

4. We tried moving to the CLI to use the documented `/approve` flow. The assistant initially suggested this invalid combination:

   ```sh
   codex resume 01a16025-dd86-7ab0-8454-293bbfd9fc36 --approve-for-me --ask-for-approval on-request
   ```

   The CLI correctly rejected it:

   ```text
   error: the argument '--approve-for-me' cannot be used with '--ask-for-approval <APPROVAL_POLICY>'
   ```

   This was a troubleshooting-command mistake, not the auto-review bug being reported. The command was corrected to:

   ```sh
   codex resume 01a16025-dd86-7ab0-8454-293bbfd9fc36 --approve-for-me
   ```

5. `/approve` was initially entered at the zsh prompt, producing:

   ```text
   zsh: no such file or directory: /approve
   ```

   We corrected this by entering it inside the Codex TUI instead.

6. The CLI update ran `npm install -g @openai/codex`, completed successfully, and requested a restart. The installed version was subsequently verified as `codex-cli 0.163.0`.

7. During resume, the CLI displayed:

   ```text
   This conversation is open in another app
   Close it there and press R to continue here.
   ```

   We followed the displayed close/retry flow and subsequently entered the conversation in the CLI.

8. Inside that resumed CLI conversation, `/approve` returned:

   ```text
   No recent auto-review denials in this thread. Denials are recorded after auto-review rejects an action.
   ```

   No original denied action was available to select.

9. We ran `/feedback`. The CLI confirmed that feedback was uploaded and supplied a GitHub issue link containing:

   ```text
   Uploaded thread: 01a16025-dd86-7ab0-8454-293bbfd9fc36
   ```

## Actual behavior

- Direct human authorization was described by auto-review as untrusted transcript content.
- Repeating explicit approval in the original implementation conversation did not resolve the denial.
- After resuming the same conversation in the CLI, `/approve` did not expose the original desktop denials.
- The blocked patch remained unapplied at the last verified state.

## Expected behavior

- Authorization supplied directly by the human user should be distinguished from instructions embedded in repository files, tool output, or relayed messages.
- If policy independently prohibits the action, the denial should identify that restriction accurately.
- The supported recovery flow should explain whether desktop denials are available after CLI resume/restart and what to do when the denial picker is empty.

## Questions for maintainers

1. Should recent auto-review denials survive a desktop-to-CLI resume of the same conversation?
2. Is `/approve` limited to denials recorded in the current process, client, or backend session?
3. Why might both a direct structured confirmation and a direct typed user authorization be described as untrusted transcript content?
4. What is the supported way to review the original denied action when `/approve` reports no recent denials?

## Feedback reference

Feedback was successfully uploaded from the CLI.

**Thread ID:** `01a16025-dd86-7ab0-8454-293bbfd9fc36`

The observations above do not establish the internal root cause. The uploaded diagnostics should help distinguish an authorization-provenance issue from a denial-retention or client-transition limitation.

items.title: Desktop: commit-message generation instantly fails when all changes are untracked

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

- Installed Windows/MSIX package: `OpenAI.Codex_26.1016.6573.0_x64`
- Desktop log release: `26.1016.51333`, build `21161`
- Desktop build commit: `28ffa59d1a9faff009b5e11511b65a65183038f1`
- Remote Codex CLI: `0.163.0`

The package and release versions above were read from the running installation and desktop logs, rather than the About dialog.

### Platform

Windows desktop app, with an existing Git repository on a Linux host connected through the app's SSH remote-project support.

### What issue are you seeing?

The built-in **Commit** flow fails **instantly** with:

> Couldn't generate a commit message

There is no generation wait or timeout. Retrying produces the same immediate failure indefinitely while the repository state stays the same.

The specific trigger identified here is that **all pending changes are untracked files**, with no staged changes or tracked-file modifications. The commit-message field is blank. With no custom commit instructions supplying context, the generator receives an empty prompt.

This is inconsistent with the actual commit operation: with **Include unstaged changes** enabled, that operation stages and commits untracked files too, but message generation omits them.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open an existing, healthy Git repository with at least one commit in Codex Desktop. The observed setup uses an SSH remote Linux repository from Windows.
2. Start with a clean index and working tree.
3. Create two small, non-ignored files in a new directory. Do not run `git add`.
4. Verify that `git status --short` shows only `??` entries, and both `git diff` and `git diff --cached` are empty.
5. Leave the commit-message field and custom Git commit instructions blank. Keep **Include unstaged changes** enabled.
6. Use the app's built-in Commit action and let it generate the message.
7. Observe the immediate error. Retry without changing Git state; the error repeats.

The original occurrence involved two new text files, so a large diff or binary-file parsing was not needed.

### Expected behavior

Automatic message generation should see the same changes that the subsequent commit operation will include, including new untracked files when **Include unstaged changes** is enabled.

If generation has no usable context, the UI should explain the missing context and offer manual message entry instead of displaying an unexplained generation failure.

### Observed behavior and why it seems intermittent

- **Only untracked additions:** immediate message-generation failure.
- **Tracked modifications plus untracked additions:** the user reports that the flow can generate a message and ultimately commit everything. The inspected implementation supports this: generation gets tracked changes, while the commit step stages both sets. Consequently, the message may omit new files it never saw.
- Asking the chat to do another turn or make more changes sometimes appears to fix the problem. Editing a tracked file or staging the additions would make the generation context nonempty; merely editing still-untracked files would not. This explains the pattern without establishing the cause of every earlier occurrence.

### Installed-code investigation

Inspection of the running installation's `app.asar` found the following path:

1. In `.vite/build/worker.js`, the `commit-message-diff` handler calls minified function `Fje`. With `includeUnstaged` enabled, it calls `l1`.
2. `l1` copies the Git index to a temporary index, runs **`git add -u`**, and collects a cached diff. Genuinely untracked files are excluded.
3. In `webview/assets/git-action-new-branch-field-eab34a12ebed.js`, `wr` passes this diff to `Zn` / `Qn`. Empty diff + empty draft + no custom instructions yields an empty prompt. The bundle explicitly contains the context note `Untracked changes are not included.`
4. In `.vite/build/src-CsH31EEu.js`, `ZJ` starts with the equivalent of:

   ```js
   const trimmed = prompt.trim();
   if (trimmed.length === 0) return null;
   ```

   This return occurs before model selection or generation telemetry.
5. The frontend maps the null/empty result to the exact reported toast.
6. In contrast, the actual `commit` handler calls `o2`, which stages tracked changes **and enumerated untracked paths**; its fallback is `git add -A`.

The key mismatch is therefore **tracked-only context collection versus tracked-and-untracked commit staging**.

### Verification and limits

- Verified the affected repository had exactly two untracked files and no tracked/staged diff.
- Reproduced the app's tracked-only diff procedure on the remote host using an isolated temporary index and temporary object directory: **0 bytes** of diff.
- Staged the two new files only in that temporary index: **2,781 bytes** of diff.
- Verified the real index bytes and repository status were unchanged afterward; the real object store was used only as an alternate read source.
- Executed the extracted installed `Zn`, `Qn`, and `ZJ` functions with stubbed model dependencies: empty context returned `null`, with **zero model-selection calls and zero generation calls**. Nonempty tracked context reached the generation stub.
- A fresh user retry still failed instantly, and the live desktop logs contained no `commit_message` generation event, consistent with the early return.

The isolated function test did not make a live model request or a real commit. No installed app files or repository staging state were changed during diagnosis. The root-cause evidence combines repository-state inspection, installed application code, deterministic isolated execution, and the observed UI failure.

### Workarounds

- Stage the intended new files before using automatic generation, for example `git add -- path/to/new-files/`.
- Enter a commit message manually, which bypasses automatic generation in the inspected commit flow.

### Related reports

- #35214 reports repeated Generate message failures; its follow-up also involves untracked files, but diagnoses an invalid `git diff --no-index` invocation rather than the empty-prompt path described here.
- #15403 includes the same toast in a staging-failure report, without this specific cause.
- #30010 concerns a different Windows/SSH temporary-index path bug, reported fixed.

This report was prepared with Codex assistance from an investigation requested by the reporter. Private repository identifiers, source contents, local user paths, credentials, and chat/thread IDs are omitted.

items.title: [Windows desktop] Chrome tab RPCs time out after 300s while getBrowser succeeds; configRequirements/read response unobserved

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

The official updater information reported `26.1013.40934`, build `20770`, prod. This is the updater's value, not an independently re-read About dialog. The actual desktop app and its child process generation were confirmed to have restarted on October 21.

### What subscription do you have?

Existing ChatGPT account; exact subscription tier not independently verified for this report.

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64.

### What issue are you seeing?

In an existing Windows desktop chat, the official Chrome-extension browser binding can be obtained quickly, but tab commands repeatedly fail with:

```text
timed out awaiting tools/call after 300s
```

An outer `timeout_ms: 1200000` does not extend that transport deadline. This blocks an authorized workflow involving six completed videos. No publication request was sent in these failing attempts.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is a captured incident and recurrence, not a deterministic minimal reproduction:

1. After the owner restarted the desktop app on October 21, tab listing, a viewport screenshot and reading an existing video editor initially succeeded.
2. A subsequent full-page screenshot hit a roughly five-second capture timeout. Tab listing and session naming later also hit the 300-second transport timeout. This sequence does not establish that the screenshot caused the later failures.
3. On October 21 at 08:50:36.492 UTC, a single `Browser.tabs.new()` began after `cua.getBrowser(...)` had completed in approximately 3.6 seconds. At 08:50:37.921 UTC, a config child logged receipt of `configRequirements/read` request 40.
4. The outer call failed at 08:55:37.796 UTC after approximately 300 seconds. No tab ID was returned. Creation is therefore UNKNOWN and was not repeated.
5. Available logs through 09:24 UTC did not show a response or natural completion for request 40. Other model-list HTTP requests in that child still returned 200; this does not prove the precise blocked stage.
6. On October 22, the three original config/REPL/launcher child processes were no longer present, while the original desktop/app-server generation remained. A different chat had working Chrome reads, so recovery was checked once in the original affected chat.
7. In that original chat, `getBrowser` again succeeded in about 1.5 seconds. A single `Browser.tabs.list()` again failed at the MCP deadline (approximately 302 seconds measured end to end). No new tab, upload, setting change or publication occurred.

### What is the expected behavior?

Existing-tab reads should return normally, or fail with a bounded, actionable error identifying the failed configuration, dispatch or response stage. An inconclusive tab-creation outcome should remain reconcilable without repeating the mutation.

### Additional information

Read-only inspection found that browser commands await managed request-header requirements before dispatch. We have not isolated whether this incident blocks there or later in Chrome dispatch/response. The missing observed config response is evidence to correlate, not a root-cause conclusion.

Related reports found during duplicate search: #45014 (older desktop build, identity/request-header dependency) and #42740 (Windows local STDIO blocking-pool exhaustion). Neither mechanism is confirmed for this incident, and the third-party policy/header fallback patch from #45014 has not been applied.

A private in-app feedback report has already been submitted by the owner. No reply has been received as of this report. Its session ID is not included here.

Please correlate configuration response delivery, managed-header preparation and browser command dispatch/response, and identify an upstream fix or supported recovery operation for the existing affected runtime. Preserving existing authentication and pending-operation outcomes is important. SDK patches, private RPCs, forced process termination and security/permission resets have not been used.

This public report excludes credentials, cookies, header values, account identifiers, local personal paths, private chat/session IDs, full transcripts and raw logs.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

OpenAI.Codex 26.1016.6573.0

### What subscription do you have?

Plus

### What platform is your computer?

x64

### What issue are you seeing?

I'm experiencing persistent **"Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model."** errors when using OpenAI Codex, despite having sufficient remaining usage quota.

The issue started around October 20, 2026, and has continued through October 22. It affects multiple Codex models, new and existing sessions, and both local and web interfaces.

**Key findings:**

- The error occurs repeatedly, preventing Codex from completing tasks.
- Switching models, creating new sessions, and retrying requests do not reliably resolve the issue.
- My Codex usage dashboard confirms that I still have available quota.
- My ChatGPT authentication is functioning normally.
- PowerShell analysis of local Codex session logs identified **69 distinct failed Session/Turn combinations** reporting `codex_error_info: server_overloaded`.
- The issue persists when accessing Codex from a South Korean IP address.

**Latest confirmed failure:**
- Timestamp: `2026-10-22T06:39:44.308Z`
- Session ID: `01a13e27-a64c-7780-93ab-d0eb15494d32`
- Turn ID: `01a16255-f5bf-7863-a555-be28e58a7d65`

This is significantly disrupting my ongoing work, and repeated retries have not resolved the problem.

I suspect a server-side capacity allocation or account-specific request routing issue, although the root cause has not been confirmed.

**Please investigate why my Codex requests consistently return `server_overloaded` despite sufficient remaining usage quota, and whether this is related to recent OpenAI service incidents affecting Codex or the South Korea region.**

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Sign in to Codex using an active ChatGPT account with sufficient remaining usage quota.
2. Open Codex on Windows (CLI or desktop interface), or access Codex through the web interface.
3. Start a new session or open an existing conversation.
4. Select any available Codex model.
5. Submit a prompt, including a simple request or an existing task.
6. Wait for Codex to process the request.
7. Codex repeatedly displays the following error:

   **"Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model."**

8. Click "Retry" or switch to another model and submit the request again.
9. The same error continues to occur, preventing the task from completing.

### Actual Behavior

- The issue occurs across multiple models and sessions.
- Both local Codex and the web interface are affected.
- The usage dashboard still shows available quota.
- The error persists despite repeated retries.
- Analysis of local session logs identified **69 distinct failed Session/Turn combinations** with `codex_error_info: server_overloaded`.
- The issue has been reproduced using a South Korean IP address.

### Expected Behavior

Codex should process requests normally when the account has sufficient remaining usage quota, without repeatedly returning server capacity errors.

### Additional Information

- **Operating System:** Windows
- **Codex CLI Version:** 0.147.0
- **ChatGPT Windows App Version:** 26.1016.6573.0
- **Affected Period:** October 20–22, 2026
- **Latest Confirmed Failure:** 2026-10-22 06:39:44 UTC
- **Error Type:** `server_overloaded`

The issue appears to be related to server-side capacity allocation or request routing rather than exhausted usage quota. The underlying cause has not yet been confirmed.

### What is the expected behavior?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

items.body:
### Problem

An optional stdio MCP server becomes ready before the first turn starts, but `tool_search` omits its tools on that first turn. The same tools appear on turn 2. This was observed with Codex 0.159.3.

### Minimal repro

1. Configure a stdio MCP server whose launch command wraps the real server with `sleep 2; exec …`.
2. Run `codex exec` with a scripted model that calls `tool_search` for one of the server's tools on its first turn.
3. Repeat through `app-server`, issuing a second turn in the same session.

### Observed

- `codex exec`: first-turn tool lookup missed in 6 of 8 runs.
- `app-server`: turn 1 missed and turn 2 found the tool in 7 of 7 runs.
- An `rmcp=trace` capture shows the server's `ListToolsResult` arriving about 3 seconds **before** the first turn begins.
- Setting `required = true` avoided the miss in 5 of 5 runs, but it makes session startup fail when this optional server is unavailable.

### Expected

Refresh the searchable tool catalog when an MCP server's `tools/list` completes, or wait briefly for servers still starting before the first turn. An optional server that is ready before turn 1 should be discoverable on turn 1.

I can provide the sanitized trace and scripted-model harness if useful.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Desktop app version `26.1016.51333`, build `21161`. Read from the installed application's Info.plist.

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected for this report.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.5. Interface language: Simplified Chinese.

### What issue are you seeing?

When starting a new Codex conversation for an existing local project, the composer header shows **“此计算机” (“This computer”)**, but the disabled send button's tooltip says:

> 请选择一个云端环境，然后继续

English equivalent: **“Select a cloud environment to continue.”**

The user reports that they can no longer create a local conversation in this project and are being directed to create/select a cloud environment instead.

The screenshot shows a local project selected, “This computer” displayed, and the cloud-environment tooltip at the same time. The selected model shown is GPT-6.1 Sol.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed user workflow, not an independently established minimal reproduction:

1. In the macOS desktop app, open the new-conversation composer for an existing local project.
2. Observe that the execution location displays “This computer.”
3. Hover over the disabled send button.
4. The tooltip requests a cloud environment despite the displayed local execution location.

Important evidence limit: the supplied screenshot was captured with an empty prompt. It establishes the contradictory execution-location/tooltip state, but does not independently establish what happens after entering a nonempty prompt. The inability to create a local conversation is user-reported. Reselecting the execution target, switching projects, and restarting have been suggested but their outcomes have not been verified.

### What is the expected behavior?

A new conversation targeting “This computer” should use local execution without requiring a published cloud environment. Its disabled-send explanation should reflect the actual blocking condition, including an empty prompt when applicable.

If local execution is unavailable because of a policy or configuration requirement, show that specific reason rather than requesting an unrelated cloud environment.

### Additional information

Observed on October 22, 2026 (UTC+08:00).

Read-only project inspection confirmed:
- The project is registered as a local project on the local host.
- Its local directory exists.
- The selected project root is not itself a Git repository. No Worktree isolation was being requested.

No controlled fresh-chat creation was performed by the diagnostic assistant, to avoid starting a duplicate task. Existing development conversations remain active.

The actual cause is unknown. A stale draft/target selection or a client-side validation mismatch are hypotheses only, not established causes.

This is a text-only, sanitized report. Private project names and paths, account identifiers, conversation contents, raw logs, and screenshots are omitted.

items.title: Prepare TUI startup to accept multiple backend sessions
items.body:
Prepare TUI startup to accept multiple backend sessions

## What changed

- Add `InitialBackendSessions` to carry the initial session and additional sessions into the TUI event loop. Existing launches continue to supply a single session.
- Shut down all supplied sessions on startup errors, cancellation, and early exits.
- Register the under-development `tui_multi_backend` feature flag, disabled by default, and expose it in the configuration schema.

## Testing

Add a regression test that fails bootstrap and verifies that both initial backends receive shutdown requests. Update multi-source event polling coverage to use the new initialization path.
