items.title: Codex 0.162.1 MXC rejects an explicit protected deny path before launching a synthetic payload

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
We observed one failed native Windows MXC admission attempt with Codex CLI 0.162.1. The intended synthetic Python payload was never created. This is a compatibility/support question about enforcing the declared policy, not a request to bypass fail-closed validation.

Recorded host metadata: Windows build 26300.9711, DisplayVersion 26H2, Home China edition. This identifies the recorded host, not a claim that a Windows Sandbox VM is available or supported on it. The desktop app version and CLI version are separate; this report concerns the explicitly selected CLI path.

The invocation explicitly selected windows.sandbox="mxc", sandbox --include-managed-config, and a named permission profile. Its policy had a default filesystem deny, explicit readonly runtime and synthetic-project paths, explicit denials below System32, and network.enabled=false.

Relevant redacted policy excerpt (not a newly executed minimal reproduction and not the full configuration):

```toml
[permissions.product-read.filesystem]
":root" = "deny"
"C:\\Windows\\System32" = "read"
"C:\\Windows\\System32\\config" = "deny"
# Other explicit runtime/project grants and protected-path denials omitted.
[permissions.product-read.network]
enabled = false
```

Observed result: Codex exited with code 1, stdout contained zero bytes, and the intended Python payload process was not observed. Stderr identified C:\Windows\System32\config in deniedPaths as an object whose identity could not be resolved; it rejected the configuration to avoid an unchecked alias bypass. No denied entry was removed, no alternate sandbox was used, and no further admission attempt was run after this failure. The diagnostic does not identify whether the unresolved identity resulted from access denial or another I/O condition; no protected-directory inspection was performed to decide that.

Source mapping:

- Codex rust-v0.162.1 maps the permission profile into MXC native grants and calls object-conflict normalization before launch: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/mxc-sandbox/src/policy.rs
- Its MXC dependency is pinned to 6cd3d58f05d3447e67109cfb75e042803b843ca4: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/Cargo.toml
- The pinned Windows resolver requests FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES and obtains the file ID; an unresolved policy path with denials present causes the observed rejection: https://github.com/microsoft/mxc/blob/6cd3d58f05d3447e67109cfb75e042803b843ca4/src/core/wxc_common/src/filesystem_object.rs
- A read-only inspection of rust-v0.163.0 found the same pinned dependency and normalization call. We have not run 0.163.0 and do not claim that every configuration fails on that version.

Requested guidance:

1. Is this strict default-deny profile with an explicit protected-system-directory denial supported on a non-elevated workload path? If unsupported, please identify the specific limitation and an officially supported contract.
2. Is there a released configuration or execution entrypoint that preserves the intended filesystem denials and disabled command networking, without modifying host DACLs, elevating the workload, removing denials, or falling back to a weaker sandbox?
3. Which version/source change and non-invasive capability evidence should an integrator require before authorizing another admission attempt?

The related elevated/ACL-update report https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/53796 concerns a different runner and failure mechanism; we are not claiming its diagnosis applies to this MXC failure.

No model turn or business Agent request was dispatched by the admission attempt. No credential contents were read or attached. This report does not claim a sandbox escape, completed business workflow, or complete application process-tree shutdown verification. Raw logs, account identifiers, private project paths, full configuration, and files are not attached.

items.title: [Dictation] Restore optional context-aware, whole-utterance transcription in ChatGPT and Codex

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

items.body:
### Summary

Please bring back the previous **record first → process the whole utterance → insert a refined final transcript** dictation experience, or at least make it a selectable mode in ChatGPT and Codex.

I am dissatisfied with the newer dictation behavior in which text is streamed into the composer word by word (or in small fragments) as I speak. For long-form prompts, I value transcription quality and semantic coherence much more than seeing the first few words immediately.

### Previous behavior vs. current behavior

**Previously:** I could dictate a long message, finish the recording, and then receive one consolidated transcription. The result appeared to benefit from the context of the *entire* utterance, including later phrases that clarify earlier ambiguous words, punctuation, or intended meaning.

**Now:** The composer shows an incremental live transcript while I am still speaking. I am concerned that early partial recognitions may become effectively fixed before later context is available, reducing the quality of long, natural dictation. This is a user-observed UX change and a quality concern, **not a claim that I have verified the underlying ASR implementation or measured an error-rate regression**.

This distinction particularly matters for longer instructions and multilingual/technical speech—for example Traditional Chinese mixed with English product names, acronyms, and technical terminology.

### Requested behavior

1. **Offer a setting to choose between two dictation modes:**
   - **Context-aware / final-only (my preference):** record the utterance, consider the complete audio and linguistic context, and insert one polished editable transcript after I stop.
   - **Live / streaming:** show provisional text while I speak for users who prioritize immediate feedback.
2. Even in the live mode, perform a **genuine final full-context transcription/revision pass** after recording ends. Earlier text, punctuation, word boundaries, and proper nouns should remain revisable based on later context; do not treat interim text as irrevocable.
3. If streaming is used internally to reduce latency, that should **not require streaming provisional text into the input box**. Backend streaming and the visible transcript presentation can be separate choices.
4. Ideally, evaluate accuracy and semantic coherence for longer prompts and code-switched languages—not only time to first displayed token.

### How to observe the change

1. Open ChatGPT or Codex and start the built-in composer microphone/dictation feature (not the operating system keyboard's dictation).
2. Dictate a multi-sentence instruction with context introduced later in the recording.
3. Observe incremental text appearing in the composer before the recording ends.
4. Compare the result and correction behavior with the earlier whole-recording, final-only dictation experience.

### Related reports

- #42078 — Similar request to restore context-aware dictation, reported specifically for **ChatGPT on iOS / Russian**. My request concerns the broader ChatGPT/Codex composer experience and keeping a whole-utterance final pass available.
- #39708 — Proposes processing audio during recording **while still inserting only a final transcript**; a good example of decoupling backend latency improvements from UI streaming.
- #23012 — Requests visible live interim text. A user-selectable mode would accommodate both preferences.

### Environment

- Affected feature: built-in ChatGPT and Codex dictation/composer microphone.
- Dictation language/use case: Traditional Chinese, including English technical terms.
- Exact app versions and platform-specific reproduction details: not captured for this report.

I would appreciate either restoring the earlier behavior or adding an explicit **context-aware dictation** option rather than making real-time, fragment-by-fragment display the only experience.

### Environment

- macOS desktop app, production channel
- Version **26.1016.61520**, build **21421**
- Built-in update check reported **up_to_date** on October 21, 2026

### Problem

Conversations assigned to an existing custom sidebar section repeatedly disappear from the visible sidebar after restarting Desktop. The original chats still exist. Supported chat inventory returns their saved section membership, numbered titles, and order.

The user has repeatedly requested individual bump messages to recover discoverability. Needing to do this after restarts is disruptive.

### Observed sequence

This is an existing-profile observation, not a clean-install or independently controlled restart reproduction:

1. Existing conversations are assigned to a custom sidebar section.
2. The user restarts the app and reports those conversations missing from the section.
3. Supported chat listing still returns the originals and their section assignments.
4. Acknowledgment-only bump messages are sent to all six current section members. All six receive and answer the messages.
5. The section membership, numbered titles, and order remain unchanged.
6. Explicit history reads for an affected original chat succeed.

Message delivery and history retrieval were verified. Final visible sidebar recovery after the latest bumps was **not independently verified**, and no post-bump restart was performed during this investigation.

### Expected behavior

Existing assigned chats should automatically load and remain discoverable in their custom section after restart, without requiring new messages. A loading failure should expose a useful retry/unavailable state and recover without silently hiding assigned entries.

### Selected diagnostic evidence

October 21 startup logs contain the following fields for chats in the affected section:

```text
method=thread/read
source=thread_hydration
error={"code":-32003,"message":"thread access denied"}
```

The same startup sequence also records:

```text
Failed to read pinned thread
errorCode=-32003
errorMessage="thread access denied"
```

Later supported direct reads and bump-message delivery succeed for the same original chats. This establishes a difference between the failing background loading path and successful direct access; it does not establish why authorization differs.

### Investigation lead — unconfirmed

Several saved section item keys use `codex:thread:local:<redacted-thread-id>`, while the live chat inventory identifies those chats with `hostId: durable`.

This is an observed identity-label mismatch, **not a proven cause**. Current supported direct reads explicitly requested with either host label both succeed and resolve to the durable chat. The failing requests' actual wire payloads and server authorization decisions were not captured.

### Previous recovery attempts and limits

- Supported section moves returned success but did not establish a lasting repair.
- An earlier backed-up edit to saved sidebar host labels did not change live readback; the user subsequently reported that restart still did not restore the entries. That edit is a diagnostic intervention, not a validated repair.
- Bumps verify access/activity but do not establish that restart loading is fixed.

Please investigate startup loading and reconciliation of custom-section entries, host/access-context resolution, and recovery after a background hydration denial. Please provide a supported recovery that preserves the original chats, history, section assignments, and active work.

### Related reports

[#51675](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51675) describes macOS durable-chat disappearance after restart with successful listing/direct reads and denied background hydration. This report adds the current build, persisted custom-section membership/order, and verified acknowledgment delivery to six original members. Please consolidate if appropriate; a shared root cause has not been established.

Only this sanitized report is submitted. No private chat titles/IDs, account details, filesystem paths, transcripts, raw logs, screenshots, or credentials are attached. Prepared and submitted by Codex at the user's request.

### What issue are you seeing?

I've noticed that my Codex CLI usage limits are being consumed abnormally fast compared to my previous experience.

Even when performing tasks of similar complexity and using Codex in a similar way, my available usage quota appears to decrease significantly faster than before.

This change is particularly noticeable with the 5-hour usage limit. I have not intentionally made any major changes to my workflow that would explain such a substantial increase in consumption.

I'm concerned that this may be related to a recent Codex update, changes in usage accounting, or a potential bug.

**Expected behavior:**
Usage limits should be consumed at a reasonably consistent rate for comparable workloads, assuming the same model and settings.

**Actual behavior:**
The available usage quota appears to decrease much faster than previously observed.

**Questions for the team:**
1. Has the usage accounting or quota consumption mechanism changed recently?
2. Is this increased consumption expected behavior?
3. Could there be a bug causing usage limits to be deducted incorrectly?

I would appreciate it if the team could investigate this issue.

**Feedback thread ID:** `01a161a7-bccb-76a3-9c82-16037a77e274`

I have already uploaded the diagnostic feedback through the Codex CLI `/feedback` command.

Thank you!

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Uploaded thread: 01a161a7-bccb-76a3-9c82-16037a77e274

### What is the expected behavior?

Usage consumption should remain reasonably consistent for comparable workloads and a reset.

### Additional information

The issue appears to be related to unexpectedly high usage consumption rather than a specific task failure.

items.body:
## Update — October 22, 2026 (Asia/Shanghai): reproduced in a new ChatGPT Work project

After the original report, I created a **new project** and reproduced the problem in **ChatGPT Work mode**. My new observations are:

- **Follow-up behavior is not reliably governed by the selected setting.** The original report below concerns Queue; the exact setting/actions in this new test still need to be documented.
- **Images cannot be read in this Work test.** The image input route (a direct attachment versus a local file), exact failure message, and whether the failure is file access or image interpretation have not yet been captured.

This adds a fresh-project reproduction and points the investigation toward **Work mode**, rather than limiting it to the original project's conversations. A new project is not a clean app profile. This update reports my subsequent test; the reviewed recording and logs below are from the earlier test and do **not** document this new Work reproduction.

The Work test's execution location (**On your computer** versus **Cloud**), exact app version, and a matched Codex comparison have not yet been recorded. Please investigate the effective follow-up setting and the image access/delivery path in Work. The two symptoms are reported together, but a shared implementation cause has not been established. This update also does not establish a connection to the separate `Broken pipe (os error 32)` error.

**How to read the earlier evidence:** both conversations in the original recording visibly showed Codex. That observation is preserved below; it should not be retroactively relabeled as a recording of this later Work test. The earlier Aeon-related code branches remain investigation leads, not a confirmed classification of either conversation.

---

## Original recorded comparison and diagnostic evidence

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

**26.1016.51333, build 21161** — ChatGPT desktop app with the Codex interface, bundle identifier `com.openai.codex`.

The version was read from the installed app's `Info.plist`. Desktop logs during the recording independently show build 21161, commit `28ffa59d1a9faff009b5e11511b65a65183038f1`. Bundled CLI package metadata reports `0.163.0-alpha.11`; the active executor version has not been independently established.

An earlier inspection the same day was on 26.1013.40934 / build 20770. The relevant code branches were checked again in build 21161; the two inspections should not be conflated.

### What subscription do you have?

**Pro**.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.4, OS build 25E246, Apple Silicon.

`uname -mprs`: `Darwin 25.4.0 arm64 arm`

Recording date: October 22, 2026, approximately 10:19:57–10:20:51, Asia/Shanghai.

### What issue are you seeing?

Two existing conversations in the same project behave differently. Both show **Codex** and **GPT-6 Astra Max**, in the same app window. **Settings → General → Follow-up behavior → Queue** is selected.

| Recorded behavior | Conversation A, affected | Conversation B, comparison |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Permissions control below the composer | Missing | Shows Full access |
| Sending a short follow-up during an active response | The message immediately appears in the transcript, without a pending queue card | The message remains in a pending card above the composer while the original response continues |
| Pending card actions | No card is shown | Steer and delete actions are visible |

The follow-up text is the same short greeting, `你好` (“hello”). A sends it twice during the active response. The recording includes pointer interactions with the Send button in both conversations; no modifier-key combination is displayed. It is not a low-level keyboard event trace.

Within this original recording, there is a conversation-specific difference in visible behavior. I previously described A as steering the current run; the directly recorded fact is immediate transcript insertion instead of a pending queue card. The exact backend submission intent for A still needs to be traced.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Using the existing conversations shown in the recording:

1. Select Codex and set Follow-up behavior to Queue.
2. Open conversation A, which has no permissions control beneath its composer.
3. Start a response. While it is still working, type `你好` and click Send.
4. Observe that the follow-up immediately appears in the transcript. Repeating it produces another transcript message, with no pending queue card visible.
5. Switch to conversation B in the same project, still using Codex and GPT-6 Astra Max.
6. Start a response and submit the same greeting with the Send button while it is working.
7. Observe the pending card with Steer/delete actions while the original response continues.
8. Open General settings: Follow-up behavior remains Queue; Send shortcut is Enter.

I recorded a 54-second reproduction; the observations above were checked against the recording. A fresh-profile sequence for creating the affected conversation has not yet been isolated. The new-project Work test described in the update above was reported later. The recording does not follow B through completion and eventual queue delivery.

### What is the expected behavior?

- A normal follow-up should wait for the current response to finish when Queue is selected.
- If a particular conversation intentionally cannot queue, disclose the effective behavior and reason before sending.
- Explain why the permissions control is unavailable for that conversation, and show its effective permissions when possible.
- Provide a supported way to restore predictable behavior without losing the conversation history.

### Additional information

#### Recording evidence

A redacted recording excerpt is prepared but **is not attached to this issue yet**. The table below summarizes the reviewed footage. It is a 24-second, silent excerpt made from the original recording, with three cuts, no speed change, and privacy masks. It is sampled at 10 fps and scaled to 1800 pixels wide; its pixels are derived from the recording, not regenerated UI.

| Original recording time | Excerpt time | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 00:06–00:19 | 00:00–00:13 | A: active response, absent permissions control, two greetings entering the transcript |
| 00:31–00:39 | 00:13–00:21 | B: Full access, a greeting retained in a pending card, Steer action |
| 00:47–00:50 | 00:21–00:24 | General settings: Queue selected, Enter send shortcut |

The original also shows that both conversations are in the same project and that the subscription is Pro. The excerpt masks the sidebar, account menu, conversation titles, and an earlier personalized greeting, so those details are documented from the original rather than independently visible in the excerpt.

#### Configuration and log corroboration

Read-only inspection verified:

```toml
[desktop]
followUpQueueMode = "queue"
```

The startup cache also contains `electron-initial-follow-up-queue-mode: "queue"`. The recording independently shows Queue selected. Persistence does not establish the final effective value used by each conversation.

At **2026-10-22 10:20:31.859 +08:00**, the desktop log records a successful `thread/queue/add` response (`errorCode=null`). This aligns with the comparison conversation's pending card in the recording. The association is based on timing; the live thread metadata could not be retrieved to independently complete that mapping. No backend submission trace establishing A's final intent was obtained.

#### Relevant code branches; root cause not established

In the installed build 21161:

- `app-initial-f3e281fb9a71.js` selects `send-only` when either `threadStartKind` or `threadSource` equals `aeon`; otherwise it reads the follow-up preference. The resolver preserves `send-only` over a queue override.
- `app-primary-9bb8fd8d770a.js` suppresses `PermissionsModeDropdown` when `isAeonActive || isAeonThread` is true. Execution mode, layout, and other conditions also affect visibility.

These are possible investigation points, **not proof that conversation A is an Aeon or executes those branches**. A navigation event during the recording reports `threadIsAeon=false`, but omits a thread identifier and cannot conclusively classify A. Exact excerpts and file hashes for the recording build are included below.

The app's `list_threads` tool still failed with `Codex app tool request failed`; earlier `read_thread` attempts also failed. These diagnostic failures limit access to live metadata; their relationship to the reported UI behavior is unknown.

Please compare effective `followUpQueueMode`, `queueModeOverride`, final submission intent, composer mode, follow-up target type, `threadStartKind`, `threadSource`, `isAeonActive`, `isAeonThread`, runtime session status, execution host, and the specific permissions-rendering condition for the two conversations.

No application settings, permissions, caches, or databases were modified by the investigation. No raw logs, account identifiers, or conversation identifiers are published in this issue.

<details>
<summary>Installed-client excerpts and SHA-256 hashes (build 21161)</summary>

`webview/assets/app-initial-f3e281fb9a71.js`

SHA-256: `a9906c234f7dfb2f59785b40f9b489d6ce509205c58ce9fd53bdfea68b1d8252`

```js
function px(e,t){return e===`aeon`||t===`aeon`}
getMessageQueueMode:async t=>{let n=e.getConversation(t.conversationId);return px(n?.threadStartKind,n?.threadSource)?`send-only`:s.readFollowUpQueueMode()}
async function s(e){let t=await r(e);return t===`send-only`?t:e.queueModeOverride??t}
```

`webview/assets/app-primary-9bb8fd8d770a.js`

SHA-256: `761037cdef242fcbf0525ceb5acd414b7c9714e30ea45402dbee7aba29cb8969`

The component takes `isAeonActive:S,isAeonThread:C`, normalizes them as `ae=S!==void 0&&S,U=C!==void 0&&C`, and derives `Se=ae||U`. The permissions-rendering condition begins:

```js
O&&!Se&&r!==`cloud`&&(!ge||Ie)?(0,wG.jsx)(Sg,
```

`Sg` imports `Gr` from app-initial, whose exported binding `cEd` dynamically loads `PermissionsModeDropdown`. These minified symbols are build-specific. This identifies a conditional branch, not the live values for either conversation.

</details>

#### Related reports

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/17445 — Queue preference ignored, including a follow-up with a persisted queue setting; open when checked earlier on October 22.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/17285 — queued messages sent before response completion; a similar symptom, not a confirmed shared cause.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/55290 — suggested by the duplicate-detection bot. Its author later withdrew the report after finding the execution-location selector and discovering the chats had been started in Cloud: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/55290#issuecomment-6281727385. This is a reason to verify execution location in the new Work test, not confirmation that it explains the follow-up or image symptoms here.

The added evidence here is the within-project comparison, the missing permissions control, the recorded send behavior, and the verified saved preference. Please consolidate with an existing tracker if appropriate.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1016.6573.0

### What subscription do you have?

plus

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11，64 位

### What issue are you seeing?

Windows 桌面应用无法识别 Microsoft Edge 标签页。

在 Settings → Computer Use 中，Edge 显示“管理”，开关已开启，但聊天输入框的 @ 菜单中没有 Edge，无法选择浏览器或读取标签页。

Edge 的 ChatGPT 扩展已安装并启用，站点访问权限为“所有网站”，只有一个浏览器配置文件，扩展侧边栏可以正常打开。

已更新应用、彻底退出并重启应用和 Edge、关闭再开启 Edge 开关，并新建 Work／Codex 聊天，问题仍然存在。

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. 在 Windows 上打开桌面应用和 Microsoft Edge。
2. 确认 Edge 中已安装并启用 ChatGPT 扩展，侧边栏可以正常打开。
3. 打开桌面应用 Settings → Computer Use，Edge 显示“管理”，开关开启。
4. 新建 Work／Codex 聊天，在输入框输入 @。
5. 菜单中没有 Edge，无法选择 Edge 或访问其标签页。

### What is the expected behavior?

Edge 应出现在聊天的 @ 菜单中，选中并授权后，应用应能够读取和操作 Edge 标签页。

### Additional information

Edge ChatGPT 扩展版本：1.26.1006.11559。

此前本机 Work 执行连接持续超时。开启代理的 TUN／虚拟网卡模式后，2026-10-21 21:09:32（UTC+8）的日志确认执行连接恢复，但 Edge 仍未出现在 @ 菜单中。

排查时，在已检查的 HKCU、HKLM 和 WOW6432Node 的 Edge NativeMessagingHosts 位置，未找到 com.openai.codexextension 注册项。尚未确认此项是否为故障原因，没有手动修改注册表。

应用 /feedback 返回的标识：
no-active-thread-01a15e99-6ae1-7f70-9e96-413fdd14d009

请协助核查浏览器发现和本机通信组件，并提供无需重新安装 Edge 扩展的修复方法。

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
### What version of the app are you using?

ChatGPT desktop app for macOS: 26.1016.61520 (build 21421), read from the currently installed application bundle.

### What subscription do you have?

Not provided.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 27.0.1, Apple Silicon (arm64).

### What issue are you seeing?

Newly created conversations do not have the project/move-to-project option in their conversation menu. Older conversations do have this option. Whether a conversation is currently running makes no difference in either case.

The user retested and observed the following:

| Conversation | Running | Project/move-to-project option |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Newly created | Yes | Missing |
| Newly created | No | Missing |
| Older | Yes | Available |
| Older | No | Available |

The exact age or creation-date boundary between affected and unaffected conversations has not been established.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Create a new conversation in the ChatGPT desktop app on macOS.
2. Open its conversation menu while it is running: the project/move-to-project option is missing.
3. After execution finishes, open the same menu again: the option is still missing.
4. Compare with an older conversation: the project/move-to-project option is available.
5. Check the older conversation both while running and while idle: the option is available in both cases.

### What is the expected behavior?

New and older conversations that are eligible for project migration should consistently expose the project/move-to-project option. If a conversation is ineligible, the app should make the restriction understandable.

### Additional information

An earlier observation suggested that fully quitting with Command+Q and reopening the app restored the option. Subsequent testing identified the new-versus-old conversation distinction above, so restarting is not being presented here as a confirmed workaround or the running state as the cause.

Drag-and-drop behavior has not been tested for this report. The cause has not been diagnosed.

Related: #51381 describes new Work sessions missing the project-move menu on Windows while older sessions retain it. This report records the macOS observation and the running/idle comparison; it may share the same underlying cause. #36464 also concerns missing project-move controls in ChatGPT Desktop.

items.title: [Feature Request] Bring ChatGPT Web Intelligent UI to Codex Desktop conversations

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

Codex Desktop App

### What feature would you like to see?

### Summary

I would love to see **ChatGPT-style Intelligent UI integrated natively into regular Codex Desktop conversations**, allowing Codex to automatically generate interactive visual explanations when appropriate.

The goal is to bring the rich, context-aware visual response experience of ChatGPT to everyday Codex conversations.

### Problem / Motivation

The new Intelligent UI experience in ChatGPT makes technical explanations significantly easier to understand through interactive diagrams, charts, controls, and visual layouts.

Codex is particularly well suited to this capability because users frequently discuss code, algorithms, system architecture, embedded systems, and complex technical concepts.

Although Codex already has some visualization capabilities through Visualize and MCP Apps, I would like this experience to become a seamless, reliable part of ordinary assistant responses.

Ideally, users should not need to explicitly invoke a specialized tool, generate a standalone HTML file, or switch to a separate viewer just to understand a technical explanation visually.

### Proposed Solution

I would like Codex Desktop to support:

1. **Automatic visual responses:** Codex should intelligently decide when a diagram, chart, or interactive component would improve an explanation, without requiring explicit instructions.
2. **Native inline rendering:** Interactive visualizations should appear directly within the assistant's response, alongside explanatory text.
3. **Interactive components:** Support diagrams, animations, charts, sliders, buttons, and other useful controls when appropriate.
4. **Conversational continuity:** Codex should be able to understand user interactions with these components and use them as context for follow-up responses.
5. **Consistent availability:** The experience should work reliably in regular Codex Desktop conversations, rather than depending on manual visualization workflows.

Simple questions should continue to receive simple text answers. Visualization should be used when it genuinely improves clarity.



### Expected Outcome

**Codex should offer the same kind of intelligent, native, interactive visual explanations that ChatGPT now provides, directly within normal conversations.**

This request is about the overall conversational experience, not simply adding another diagram-generation tool.

Thank you for considering this feature!

### Additional information

### Environment

- Product: Codex Desktop App
- Platform: Windows 10
- Request type: Feature enhancement / UX improvement

### Related Issues

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51817 — Request to make Intelligent UI available in Dot conversations.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/36660 — Proposal for inline visualization rendering in the Codex TUI.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/33164 — Existing Visualize skill behavior and invocation issues.

### Scope Clarification

I understand that Codex already has some visualization capabilities.

This request is specifically about making **ChatGPT-style Intelligent UI a first-class, automatically available experience in regular Codex Desktop assistant responses**.

The desired behavior is broader than manually invoking Visualize, rendering a Mermaid diagram, or opening an MCP App canvas.

Ideally, the experience should feel as natural and integrated as it does in ChatGPT.

labels.name: bug

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.163.0

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT (tier omitted; not relevant to a local TUI check)

### Which model were you using?

Not relevant: the edit is refused locally before any request is sent

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Windows Terminal, PowerShell

### Codex doctor report

not included; the relevant thread state is summarized below

### What issue are you seeing?

After resuming a thread whose history contains a steer, editing a later prompt with Esc-Esc fails:

```text
■ Failed to edit the selected prompt: the selected transcript prompt no longer matches the persisted thread
```

The thread itself is healthy: it answers new turns, and `thread/revert` to the same turn succeeds.

Related but distinct from #38865. There the steer is visible and selecting it hits the steer guard. Here the steer is **not** visible, so every prompt after it is off by one.

### Root cause (as far as traced)

`backtrack_revert_before_turn_id` (`codex-rs/tui/src/app_backtrack.rs`) resolves the selection by its ordinal among visible user messages, counted from `transcript_cells` in the TUI, against **every** `UserMessage` in the hydrated persisted turns, steers included. It then requires the text at that ordinal to equal the selected prompt.

A steer is committed into the running turn as that turn's second `UserMessage`. The summary turn view does not carry it. On the affected thread, `thread/turns/list` returns:

| turn | summary view (default) user messages | `itemsView: "full"` user messages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| T1 (interrupted) | P1 | P1, **P2 (steer)** |
| T2 (completed) | P3 | P3 |
| T3 (interrupted) | P2 resent | P2 resent |

If the resumed transcript draws T1 from the summary, as its one-prompt shape suggests, selecting T3's prompt (visible ordinal *k*) then resolves ordinal *k* in the full thread to P3. Because P3 is not equal to "P2 resent", the edit is refused. Selecting T2's prompt fails the same way against the steer and reports the steer error.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Send prompt P1 and, while the turn runs, send P2 so that it is committed as a steer into the same turn; interrupt.
2. Send P3 and let it complete.
3. Send another prompt P4.
4. Quit and `codex resume <thread>`. The pre-resume turns render from the paginated summary.
5. Esc-Esc, select P4, Enter. The edit fails with the message above. Prompts before the steer still edit fine.

These steps are reconstructed from the affected thread data and have not been re-run on a fresh thread yet. Thread id available on request.

### What is the expected behavior?

The edit resolves the prompt the user selected. Two ways to get there: count visible prompts against the same projection the transcript was drawn from, or match by item id or `client_id` instead of by ordinal. Either way, a steer that is hidden in the transcript should not shift later prompts.

### Additional information

The app-server path works. `thread/revert { beforeTurnId: T3 }` dropped exactly the intended turns, and `thread/turns/list` afterwards showed T2 as the newest turn.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

App version: not stated in the incident record.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro for the native OpenAI models, plus a dedicated OpenRouter API key for Jev.

### What platform is your computer?

Codex Desktop. Operating system version: not stated in the incident record.

### What issue are you seeing?

I wanted Astra, Sol and Luna on native OpenAI through my ChatGPT account, plus only Jev through a dedicated OpenRouter key. Jev is the additional model I wanted to access through OpenRouter.

OBSERVED menu changes: a menu containing only Jev, then a catalog of 458 OpenRouter entries, then 220 entries after pruning. Pruning did not restore provider isolation.

A temporary experiment with OpenRouter as the default had been explicitly authorized. That did not establish that later coexistence of the native routes and Jev worked. Troubleshooting continued inside chats using OpenRouter while saved default changes were presented as progress toward native routing.

The assistant then removed the provider definition before migrating the chats that depended on it. Resuming those chats produced:

```
Model provider 'openrouter' not found
```

Recovery restored the affected histories to a native OpenAI route and reopened the chats, but the promised Jev dropdown entry remained absent. No evidence establishes that downloading or listing model names itself caused the recorded usage.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

These steps summarize the recorded configuration and failure sequence. The incident record does not document a fresh controlled replay.

* Retain native OpenAI models through the ChatGPT account and define an extra OpenRouter provider for Jev only.
* Ask Codex for a combined menu containing Astra, Sol and Luna on native OpenAI and Jev on its dedicated OpenRouter key. Check whether the delivered menu preserves those routes rather than replacing them with an OpenRouter catalog.
* Continue a chat that uses the OpenRouter provider, then remove its provider definition without first migrating that chat to a valid route.
* Resume the chat and check for `Model provider 'openrouter' not found`.

### What is the expected behavior?

Keep model identity, provider identity and credentials separate. Preserve native OpenAI authentication for the native models and use the dedicated OpenRouter key only for Jev. Verify the requested menu and its routes in the Desktop UI before reporting the result complete.

Before removing a provider definition, identify the chats that depend on it and preserve a valid route for each affected chat. A change to a saved default is distinct from migration of an existing chat.

### Additional information

OBSERVED response windows, rounded to whole minutes: 78 minutes and 28 minutes. ESTIMATED additional recovery: about 20 minutes by a later recorded snapshot, with recovery continuing afterward. These timestamped spans do not measure continuous user labor or establish how much time was wasted.

OBSERVED cumulative workload: 53,865,825 token units in the affected chats, including cached input. OBSERVED separate native recovery workload: 3,631,997 cumulative token units at its recorded snapshot. Subsequent recovery work is excluded.

These counts describe workload. They do not measure how many tokens were avoidable.

Evidence: private incident record dated 2026-09-27.

Related issue: [#46348](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/46348). State: OPEN. It requests provider neutral sessions with hot provider switching and cold resume without forking.

Related issue: [#29156](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/29156). State: OPEN. It reports that Codex Desktop cannot offer custom provider models in the model picker while keeping existing chats, and that the available paths replace the built in catalog. This report adds a specific assistant workflow on that surface: the provider definition was removed before dependent chats were migrated, and saved default changes were presented as progress toward native routing while the requested menu was still missing.

items.title: [macOS] Chinese IME drops first letter in floating chat when right-side tab is full-screen and a suggested prompt is visible

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1016.61520 (build 21421, prod channel). The app's update checker reports this installation is up to date. The issue persists after updating.

### What subscription do you have?

Not provided.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS, Apple Silicon. `uname -mprs`: `Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm`.

### What issue are you seeing?

The first pinyin letter is dropped from Chinese IME composition in the floating chat composer at the bottom right, under this specific combination of UI conditions:

- The right-side content tab (for example, a Markdown document preview) is expanded into its in-app full-screen view.
- The conversation is shown as a floating mini chat window at the bottom right.
- A suggested prompt is visible in the composer.

To clarify, “full-screen” here means the **right-side tab's full-screen/expanded view within Codex**, not macOS's native full-screen mode for the entire application.

When typing `nihao` to enter `你好`, the initial `n` disappears and the active IME composition contains only `ihao`. The candidate list consequently offers incorrect candidates such as `哦好` rather than the intended `你好`.

This also happens after explicitly clicking the editable input area and confirming that the caret is blinking before typing. It is therefore not explained by simply starting to type without first clicking the input box.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Open a content tab in the right-side panel, such as a Markdown document preview.
2. Expand that right-side tab into its in-app full-screen view.
3. Keep the conversation in the floating mini chat window at the bottom right.
4. Wait until a suggested prompt is visible in the composer.
5. Click the composer input area and verify that the caret is blinking.
6. With a Chinese pinyin IME active, type `nihao` to compose `你好`.
7. Observe that the first letter `n` is missing: the IME composition shows `ihao` and the candidates are incorrect.

The reporter identifies the combination of tab full-screen view, floating conversation, and a visible suggested prompt as the necessary conditions for reproducing the issue. A complete matrix of negative controls has not been recorded.

### What is the expected behavior?

The composer should preserve all keystrokes from the start of IME composition. Typing `nihao` should produce the full pinyin composition `nihao` and the expected candidate `你好`, including when a suggested prompt is visible.

### Additional information

- Updating to the currently available latest app version did not resolve the issue.
- The exact input method product/version has not been confirmed.
- The reporter provided a screenshot showing the active composition `ihao` and the incorrect candidate list. The screenshot is not attached here because it also contains unrelated private workspace content.
- Reproduction details are reported by the affected user; an automated agent has not independently reproduced the UI interaction.
- The interaction between the suggested prompt and the start of IME composition may be relevant, but no root cause has been established.

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.163.0`

### What subscription do you have?

Not relevant. This is a local configuration command.

### Which model were you using?

Not relevant. The command does not start a model turn.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x86_64

### What terminal emulator and version are you using?

zsh 5.9. The terminal does not matter here because the command is non-interactive.

### Codex doctor report

Not included because this reproduction uses an isolated `CODEX_HOME` and does not depend on machine state.

### What issue are you seeing?

`codex mcp get docs --json` omits `required` when the server is configured with `required = true`. The command exits successfully and prints the other server settings, so users and scripts cannot determine from this output whether the server is required.

The CLI reference says this command prints the raw config entry: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/cli/reference

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Run this with Codex CLI 0.163.0:

```sh
test_home="$(mktemp -d)" && printf '%s\n' '[mcp_servers.docs]' 'command = "printf"' 'required = true' > "$test_home/config.toml" && CODEX_HOME="$test_home" codex mcp get docs --json
```

The output is:

```json
{
  "name": "docs",
  "enabled": true,
  "disabled_reason": null,
  "transport": {
    "type": "stdio",
    "command": "printf",
    "args": [],
    "env": null,
    "env_vars": [],
    "cwd": null
  },
  "enabled_tools": null,
  "disabled_tools": null,
  "startup_timeout_sec": null,
  "tool_timeout_sec": null
}
```

`required` is absent.

### What is the expected behavior?

The JSON should include the configured value:

```json
"required": true
```

### Additional information

`McpServerConfig` retains this value in `codex-rs/config/src/mcp_types.rs:244-248`:

https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2a77e82f09212c9e1bbf02656afca5d8172c5f9e/codex-rs/config/src/mcp_types.rs#L244-L248

`run_get` manually builds the JSON object in `codex-rs/cli/src/mcp_cmd.rs:999-1012` and does not copy `server.required`:

https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2a77e82f09212c9e1bbf02656afca5d8172c5f9e/codex-rs/cli/src/mcp_cmd.rs#L999-L1012

The smallest fix is to add `"required": server.required` to that object and cover it with an integration test that loads `required = true` and checks the JSON output.

items.title: Require managed configuration from the configured server
items.body:
Require managed configuration from the configured server

## Why

Local administrators need to require managed configuration from a specific customer-hosted server before a session can start.

## What changed

- Add a local managed `config_server` requirement with an HTTPS base URL and optional OAuth settings. Validate endpoints and derive the bundle route as `codex/config/bundle` beneath the base URL.
- Replace the entire `config_server` block when a higher-priority requirements layer supplies one, keeping the endpoint and OAuth settings together. Reject this setting in fetched policy.
- Track the applied server through configuration snapshots, role overrides, and refreshes. Reject session startup and managed refreshes when the applied server does not match the requirement; user refreshes retain the session's managed configuration.

## Testing

Add coverage for missing, mismatched, and matching server configuration at session startup, whole-block replacement, rejection of server settings in fetched policy, and preservation across role overrides and refreshes.

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: extension
labels.description: Issues related to the VS Code extension

items.body:
### What version of the IDE extension are you using?

Codex extension version:  26.1007.21434

### What subscription do you have?

Base.

### Which IDE are you using?

VS Code

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.9807 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

The Codex VS Code extension has a relatively large installation footprint. The extension package and associated binaries consume significant disk space compared to many other AI-assisted coding extensions.

This can increase:
- Installation time
- Update download size
- Disk usage
- Bandwidth consumption on metered networks

At Present Codex also include both windows x64 and Linux x64 instead of Winodws only.

Please consider reducing the package size where possible.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Install the Codex VS Code extension.
2. Check the extension's installed size on disk.
3. Compare it with other AI coding extensions.
4. Observe that the storage footprint is relatively large.

This is a feature request rather than a functional bug.

### What is the expected behavior?

The extension should have a smaller installation footprint through optimizations such as:

- Removing unused dependencies
- Better bundling and tree-shaking
- Compressing packaged assets
- Shipping only required platform-specific binaries
- Downloading optional components on demand
- Providing a lightweight/minimal installation option

### Additional information

A smaller extension would provide several benefits:

- Faster installation
- Faster updates
- Reduced storage consumption
- Reduced bandwidth usage
- Better experience on low-storage devices and metered connections

Thank you for considering this enhancement.

I also wanted to ask whether it would be possible to receive a one-time complimentary reset of my Codex usage limits or some additional usage credits.

I completely understand if this isn't possible, but I'd really appreciate your consideration!

Thank you for building such a great tool.

Best regards,
An active Codex user and UX/UI designer

items.body:
### 问题描述

在 Windows Codex 桌面应用中，我明确授权助手通过官方 Chrome 集成打开 https://mms.pinduoduo.com 。首次打开返回导航超时，随后获取同一标签页时收到 site-safety policy 拒绝。未获得页面内容，也未出现网站授权提示或 Auto-review。

本次仅请求打开页面，未涉及购买、付款、广告投放、上传或账号修改。

### 原始报错（已隐去标签页编号）

首次打开：

`Timed out waiting for tab [redacted] to navigate to https://mms.pinduoduo.com.`

随后获取标签页：

> Browser Use rejected this action due to browser security policy. Reason: The site-safety policy blocks this action; no user permission prompt or Auto-review was attempted. Browser use could not acquire authority to observe page content. The site safety gate did not grant access for https://mms.pinduoduo.com. Site safety policy blocked this URL. The agent must not attempt to achieve the same outcome via workaround, indirect execution, raw CDP or browser commands, alternate browser surfaces, or policy circumvention. Proceed only with a materially safer alternative that does not require this blocked browser action; if none exists, stop and request user input.

### 环境

- Windows 桌面应用，官方 Chrome 扩展连接。
- 最新本地连接注册记录引用 Windows 安装包目录版本 26.1016.6573.0；未通过“关于”页面独立核实。
- Browser、Chrome、Computer Use、Unified Computer Use 插件版本：26.1016.51333。
- Chrome 配置指向的 ChatGPT 扩展版本：1.26.1015.10801。
- 本次会话观察记录；未执行干净配置或全新安装复现。

### 已完成的只读排查

| 项目 | 观察结果 |
| --- | --- |
| 官方插件 | Browser、Chrome、Computer Use、Unified Computer Use 均已安装并启用，版本一致 |
| CLI 路径 | 用户、系统及检查用命令进程未设置 CODEX_CLI_PATH 环境变量；配置中的 CLI 文件存在 |
| 运行依赖 | 配置引用的 Node、Node REPL、CUA 入口文件均存在 |
| Chrome 本地连接注册 | 两处注册文件的最新记录版本一致，最新记录引用路径均存在 |
| Windows 代理 | 手动代理关闭；配置了 PAC，PAC 地址返回 HTTP 200 |
| 本地代理端口 | 保留的本地代理端口正在监听，但手动代理关闭 |
| 实际进程代理环境 | 只读检查 Codex 桌面主进程、18 个 cua_repl、47 个 node_repl 及 Chrome 扩展辅助进程；HTTP_PROXY、HTTPS_PROXY、ALL_PROXY、NO_PROXY、NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY 均未设置 |
| 继承判断 | 父进程本身也无代理变量，不符合“父进程有代理变量、子进程漏继承”的已知案例 |
| 连接快照 | 所检查 Codex/Node 辅助进程有 20 条远端 443 连接，未连接上述本地代理端口；此快照不证明具体安全请求的路径 |
| 基础 HTTPS | 使用配套 Node 向 https://developers.openai.com/ 发起 HEAD 请求，约 1.8 秒返回 HTTP 200；不代表站点安全服务已通过验证 |
| 近期连接日志 | 所检查日志未找到代理超时、连接拒绝、nodeRepl.fetch request failed 或 Debugger unattached |
| 安全判定日志 | 最近 48 小时桌面日志及本地日志数据库未找到 pinduoduo、site_status、site-safety 或 site safety 相关记录；浏览器会话/插件目录检查未获得更具体错误 |

以上结果未确定拒绝根因，不能区分有意限制、误分类或安全服务异常。PAC 与环境变量属于不同机制，变量为空本身不证明代理异常。

### 请求协助

1. 请确认 mms.pinduoduo.com 的拒绝是否属于有意限制，或存在分类/权限判定异常。
2. 请说明判定范围及可公开的原因类别，并提供受支持的复核或恢复流程。
3. 如需进一步诊断，请告知官方私密渠道及所需关联编号/日志。
4. 建议为拒绝提供可操作的说明及反馈关联编号，以便区分本地连接故障。

items.title: Support configured credential providers in remote execution
items.body:
Support configured credential providers in remote execution

## Why

Remote credential masking previously fell back to unmasked execution whenever custom credential providers were configured.

## What changed

- Transport configured provider rules to the executor-local network proxy, where credential values and destination context are resolved.
- Advertise `credentialMaskingCustomProviders` and negotiate masking support. Keep the warning and unmasked fallback for executors that support only built-in providers.
- Discard provider rules when masking is disabled and omit their contents from debug output.

## Testing

Extend coverage for capability compatibility, provider configuration round trips, and fallback on older executors. Exercise configured-provider masking in remote request history and verify that masked placeholders are restored to real credentials in upstream request headers.

items.title: [Enhancement] Review a bounded dependency-preparation manifest before package-manager execution

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

items.body:
## Request
Provide a supported dependency-preparation workflow that makes installation scope inspectable before execution rather than treating every package-manager command as an opaque shell action. This is a feature proposal, not a claim that all installs are blocked or safe.

## Manifest
For an explicitly requested development task, expose target environment/directory, versions and lockfile identity, registries, cache/output paths, executable build/lifecycle hooks, network destinations/data categories, enforceable resource/time limits, cleanup plan, and whether existing packages are replaced.

Prefer isolated project environments. System-wide installation, persistent-environment replacement, registry changes, credential access and broader writes require separate scope evaluation.

## Acceptance criteria
- Grant only effects permitted by applicable policy.
- Lockfile, registry, environment or executable-hook changes invalidate relevant authorization.
- Bounded retries cannot silently broaden scope.
- Unsupported resource limits are disclosed, not claimed enforced.
- Refusal identifies the missing capability or disallowed effect.
- Execution remains sandboxed and reviewed; a manifest is not blanket permission for arbitrary pip/npm/shell code.

Related: #1457 concerns historical uv sandbox failures; #37677 concerns unauthorized persistent-environment replacement. This requests a scoped preparation interface, not another report of either bug. Routine setup should not force a choice between ambiguous repeated prompts and broad access. Please consolidate if an equivalent workflow is already planned.

items.title: [Enhancement] Ground approval-blocked status in harness events, separating planning pauses from AutoReview denials

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

items.body:
## Request
Expose a machine-owned blocker-origin field in task status and conversation UI. An assistant deciding not to submit a command should not be indistinguishable from a command rejected by AutoReview. This is an observability enhancement, not a newly reproduced reviewer defect.

## Proposed contract
Distinguish `not_submitted` (assistant planning concern), `approval_pending`, `review_denied`, `review_unavailable`, `execution_policy_rejected`, `execution_failed` (process started), and `unknown`.

Expose a privacy-safe event reference, timestamp, execution context and supported next action where available. Assistant-authored summaries must not manufacture a reviewer event. Display uncertainty rather than inventing a reason.

## Acceptance tests
- A pause before any tool call produces no AutoReview-denied badge.
- A reviewer denial links to its actual decision.
- Reviewer timeout and process failure remain distinct.
- Resume, compaction and delegation retain provenance rather than turning old narrative into a new denial.
- Public diagnostic export excludes prompts, private paths, credentials and sensitive arguments.

Related: #34898 covers self-generated governance loops; #43633 covers opaque policy rejection. This specifically requests trustworthy blocker attribution, not removal of safeguards or legitimate clarification. An assistant should not be able to blame an invisible security system for its own decision. Please consolidate if this exact status contract is already tracked.

This report requests a supported diagnostic and recovery path, not a safeguard bypass. Related reports include #54746 and #55165; a shared cause has not been established.

```
requestApprovalPolicy=never
requestApprovalsReviewer=user
requestPermissionProfile=:danger-full-access
resolvedApprovalPolicy=never
resolvedApprovalsReviewer=user
```
Personal paths and conversation identifiers are omitted.

Read-only configuration inspection found a trusted project entry, no explicit approval/sandbox setting in the inspected user config, no requirements.toml at the inspected default user location, and no project .codex/config.toml. The inspected local rules contain an older exact-prefix allow entry, but this is NOT evidence that the current rejected calls match that entry or that higher-priority policy permits them.

A bounded search of desktop logs from October 21–22 did not recover the rejection itself. Accessible retained task records describe the API and frontend startup rejections but do not retain the complete original rejected arguments. Therefore the precise rejecting layer and a minimal reproducer are currently UNKNOWN.

## Expected / requested guidance
1. How can the app expose the enforcing component, matched rule or privacy-safe decision ID for this generic pre-execution denial?
2. What supported diagnostic collection is available when the task has approval_policy=never and no command-approval or feedback-submission tool is exposed?
3. If this narrowly scoped localhost startup is permitted, what is the official recovery path without changing security settings or moving the denied operation to another tool?

## Environment and limitations
Windows desktop app, PowerShell, local workspace and existing local synthetic database. Installed app version has not yet been verified for this report; desktop app and standalone CLI versions must not be conflated.
This is an observed failure report, not a newly executed minimal reproduction. The denied operations have not been replayed for this report; no policy files were changed. Full access is not asserted to override other restrictions.

Enable executor cleanup hooks with V2 capability discovery

## Why

Executor hooks depended on V1 discovery snapshots, so plugins discovered through V2 could not run their cleanup hooks.

## What changed

Prepare executor hook sources during step setup from either V1 or V2 discovery and capture them in `StepContext` for stop, interrupt, and memory consolidation hooks. Restrict V2 sources to selected plugin installations while preserving plugin enablement, hook admission, MCP routing, and app tool policy checks.

## Testing

Add unit coverage for V2 hook admission, environment routing, disabled plugins, and failed discovery. Add integration coverage showing that `Stop` and `Interrupt` cleanup hooks run with V2 discovery alone and remain silent when the plugin is disabled.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1013.40934 (build 20770), bundle id `com.openai.codex`, read from the installed app bundle.
Computer Use helper: 26.1013.1001501 (build 1001501).
Authorization plug-in `CodexComputerUseAuthorizationPlugin`: 0.1.0 (build 857).

### What subscription do you have?

Not included.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 27.0.1 (26A434)

`Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm`

### What issue are you seeing?

Unlocking an already logged-in Mac left the lock-screen spinner running for 11 minutes 41 seconds. This was a lock-screen unlock, not a boot login and not a login after logout. The Mac was not rebooted and the session was not logged out.

Times below are China Standard Time (UTC+8) on 2026-10-21.

- 19:52: the screen locked.
- 20:29:18: `authd` entered `CodexComputerUseAuthorizationPlugin:allow` and stayed there.
- 20:40:59: the plug-in finally logged `socket response=DENY`.
- Immediately after that, `system.login.screensaver` succeeded and `loginwindow` unlocked the screen.

Password verification failed at 20:29:18 and again at 20:30:21. The spinner still did not clear. The whole authorization waits for the plug-in to return, so a failed password cannot be shown until the socket responds.

Please do not let a plug-in failure, or a socket that is slow to answer, block `loginwindow`. If the plug-in cannot decide, it should fail or time out so the lock screen can show the password result and continue the normal unlock path.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Use a Mac that is already in a graphical session. This was not a cold boot.
2. Lock the screen. This lock happened at 19:52 CST.
3. Submit the lock-screen password. At 20:29:18 CST, `authd` started `CodexComputerUseAuthorizationPlugin:allow` for `system.login.screensaver`.
4. The spinner stays up until the plug-in finishes reading its login-authorization socket. In this case that was 20:40:59 CST, when the socket returned `DENY`.

### What is the expected behavior?

The authorization plug-in should not hold the lock-screen spinner until its socket returns. A timeout or a plug-in failure should release `loginwindow` immediately. A failed password check should be shown without waiting for that socket.

### Additional information

Component: Codex app / Computer Use / macOS authorization plug-in on the lock-screen unlock path.

Related: #29616, #26319, #55806. This report is a password unlock on macOS 27.0.1 with plug-in build 857. The mechanism did not finish until the socket returned `DENY`.

These plug-in lines were copied from `log show` on this Mac during the incident. A repeat `log show` the next morning no longer returned the same debug lines.

```
2026-10-21 20:40:59.996 Df SecurityAgentHelper-arm64[67675:14a1e4e] [com.openai.sky.CUAService.AuthorizationPlugin:authorization] MechanismDestroy called
```

items.title: [macOS Chat 26.1016] Sending a follow-up makes completed answer disappear; only “Worked for” remains

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
## Summary

In the **ChatGPT/Codex macOS desktop app, ordinary Chat mode**, a **completed and previously visible final assistant answer disappears immediately after the user sends the next message in the same conversation**. The earlier turn is left showing only its collapsed `Worked for …` duration, even though the user's earlier prompt, attachments, and subsequent turns remain visible.

The affected answer was a detailed CV review and application-preparation response with generated PDF/Word file links. It took approximately **6m 13s** to generate. The user had not finished reading or downloading it before it vanished.

**Key distinction:** The user did not navigate away or switch conversations to trigger this incident. Sending an ordinary next message in the **same chat** was sufficient.

## Environment

- Surface: Ordinary Chat in the unified ChatGPT/Codex desktop app (not CLI, IDE extension, or a local Codex task)
- Platform: macOS, Apple Silicon (arm64)
- Observed client identifier: `Codex Desktop/26.1016.51333`. The About-dialog version was not independently verified
- Date observed: October 22, 2026
- Occurrence: Intermittent but recurring in the affected conversation; not known to happen on every message
- Exact macOS version and model settings: Not independently verified

## Steps to reproduce (user-observed sequence)

1. Continue an existing ordinary Chat conversation in the macOS desktop app.
2. Upload several PDF documents and request a detailed comparison and tailored downloadable deliverables.
3. Let the assistant finish its answer. The UI shows a substantive completed response below `Worked for 6m 13s`, with PDF/DOCX links.
4. Send an ordinary follow-up question **in the same conversation**.
5. Scroll back to the preceding assistant turn. The completed final-answer body has disappeared; only `Worked for 6m 13s` remains. Earlier user attachments and messages are still there.
6. Other subsequent assistant replies can appear normally, but this loss of earlier completed replies has recurred.

This is a user-observed intermittent sequence, not a deterministic minimal test. A screenshot of the missing-answer state was captured but is withheld from this public report because it contains private conversation material.

## Expected

Completed final assistant answers, including generated-file links, should remain visible and accessible when the user continues the same conversation. If recovery is required, the UI should communicate the problem and provide a non-destructive way to retry loading.

## Actual and impact

- The earlier final answer disappears while the elapsed-time/activity section remains.
- The user loses access to completed research, document analysis, and download links before reading or saving the result.
- Reconstructing completed work by asking again is not an acceptable recovery path in a core multi-turn conversation product.
- This substantially undermines confidence in ChatGPT as a reliable place for extended work.

**Root cause is unknown in this occurrence.** We did not inspect conversation persistence metadata or test whether a new window recovers the answer. It may be a rendering problem or a persistence/synchronization issue. Neither is asserted as established fact.

## Related issues

- #55915: Particularly close report on macOS with the same **next-user-turn** trigger, plus API evidence in that reporter's environment that completed final nodes may be flagged `can_save:false` and subsequently removed. This report does not claim to have confirmed that signature.
- #53540: Same next-user-turn trigger and retained Thinking summary on ChatGPT Web.
- #52204: Missing macOS Chat answer below `Worked for`, with a different navigation/reopen sequence. Additional evidence for this occurrence was posted in [a comment there](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/52204#issuecomment-6330371868).
- #52493: Windows desktop report of completed answers missing on chat revisit while duration metadata remains.

Please merge or mark duplicate if these share a confirmed defect, but retain the **same-chat next-message trigger** and **lost deliverable links** as reproduction details.

## Requested action

1. Investigate and regression-test the transition from an already completed final answer to an ordinary next-user-turn in macOS Chat, especially after long, tool-heavy responses.
2. Verify whether affected final messages remain persisted or are removed; specifically evaluate whether #55915's hidden / `can_save:false` state could apply.
3. Prevent the UI from silently presenting a finished assistant turn without its answer.
4. Provide a recoverable missing-message state and protect generated-file links from being effectively lost on the next user turn.
5. Route to the owning ChatGPT product team if this public repo is not the correct tracking surface.

No account identifiers, private document filenames, conversation URLs/IDs, personal paths, or unredacted screenshots are included.
